Accordion

components-accordion · ./src/components/accordion.stories.gts
An accordion component is an element that organizes content into collapsible sections, enabling users to expand or collapse them for efficient information presentation and navigation. The yielded `Item` is already bound to its accordion: pass each one a `@title` and its content as the block.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@align` | `"start" \| "end"` |  |  |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Size of the accordion. When not set, no size class is applied (matching |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `AccordionItem` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLUListElement`.

AccordionSkeleton

components-accordion-accordionskeleton · ./src/components/accordion-skeleton.stories.gts
A loading placeholder for an `Accordion`: `@count` items, with the first one open unless `@open` is `false`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"start" \| "end"` |  | Which side the chevrons sit on. Defaults to `end`. |
| `@count` | `number` |  | How many items to show. Defaults to 4. |
| `@isFlush` | `boolean` |  | Removes the items' side padding, unless `@align` is `start`. |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Shows the first item open. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@ordered` | `boolean` |  | Renders an `<ol>` in place of a `<ul>`. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLUListElement | HTMLOListElement`.

AiChatCard

ai-chat-card · ./src/components/ai-chat/card.stories.gts
`AiChatCard` is a card container for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat), typically rendered inside a message in `ChatShell`'s `<:messages>` block. Content is supplied through `<:header>`, `<:media>`, `<:body>`, `<:footer>` (commonly an `AiChatCardFooter`), and `<:decorator>` named blocks.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@isLayered` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, follows Carbon's layered-tile styling instead of the chat shell's default background. |
| `@isFlush` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, removes the default padding, useful when the card is used as a container for content that needs to be flush against its edges. |

## Blocks

- `<:header>`: Upstream `header` slot.
- `<:media>`: Upstream `media` slot.
- `<:body>`: Upstream `body` slot.
- `<:footer>`: Upstream `footer` slot — typically an `<AiChatCardFooter>`.
- `<:decorator>`: Upstream `decorator` slot.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

AiChatCardFooter

ai-chat-card-card-footer · ./src/components/ai-chat/card-footer.stories.gts
`AiChatCardFooter` renders a row of action buttons for an `AiChatCard`'s `<:footer>` block, driven entirely by an `@actions` array rather than yielded content. When every action's `label` is empty, it switches to a row of icon-only ghost buttons instead of labeled buttons — matching upstream's own derivation. Each action's `kind` maps onto this addon's `Button` component (`'primary'`, `'secondary'`, `'tertiary'`, `'ghost'`, or `'danger'`); `@onAction` is called with the clicked action whenever a button is pressed.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@actions` | `CardFooterAction[]` |  |  |
| `@onAction` | `(action: CardFooterAction) => void` |  |  |

## Element

AiChatCardSteps

ai-chat-card-preview-card · ./src/components/ai-chat/card-steps.stories.gts
`AiChatCardSteps` renders a vertical list of steps — e.g. an agent's reasoning or progress trail — for use inside an `AiChatCard`'s `<:body>` block. Each step's `kind` is one of `IconIndicator`'s kinds (`'failed'`, `'caution-major'`, `'caution-minor'`, `'undefined'`, `'succeeded'`, `'normal'`, `'in-progress'`, `'incomplete'`, `'not-started'`, `'pending'`, `'unknown'`, `'informative'`); `'in-progress'` renders a spinner instead of an icon. A step with no `kind` renders only its `label`. The other stories here mirror upstream's preview-card compositions of `AiChatCard`, `AiChatCardFooter`, `Toolbar` and `AiChatCardSteps`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@steps` | `CardStep[]` |  |  |

AiChatChatButton

ai-chat-chat-button · ./src/components/ai-chat/chat-button.stories.gts
`AiChatChatButton` is a button styled for AI Chat surfaces: a taller pill radius than this addon's plain `Button`, plus an `@isQuickAction` variant (a small, outlined chip used for quick-reply-style options) that can be marked `@isSelected` once chosen. Exported as `AiChatChatButton` because Carbon React has its own (not yet implemented) `ChatButton`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@kind` | `ChatButtonKind` |  | Button kind. Defaults to `'primary'` (or `'ghost'` when `@isQuickAction` is set and no kind is given). |
| `@size` | `ChatButtonSize` |  | Button size. Defaults to `'lg'` (or `'sm'` when `@isQuickAction` is set). |
| `@isQuickAction` | `boolean` |  | Renders as a small, pill-shaped quick-action chip rather than a full-size button. |
| `@isSelected` | `boolean` |  | Marks a quick-action chip as the currently-selected option. Blocks both user interaction and programmatic clicks (via `inert` plus a capture- phase click guard), matching upstream's behavior. Only takes effect when `@isQuickAction` is set - upstream's own normalization only applies it on that branch. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onClick` | `() => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLButtonElement`.

AiChatCodeSnippet

ai-chat-code-snippet · ./src/components/ai-chat/code-snippet.stories.gts
`AiChatCodeSnippet` is a CodeMirror 6 powered code display/editor: syntax highlighting, line folding, and a collapse/expand affordance for long snippets. Exported as `AiChatCodeSnippet` (an existing Carbon React `CodeSnippet` already occupies the plain name). `@code` is the sole content source — pass a plain string (update it however you like, e.g. token by token while streaming a response) and the editor stays in sync via a throttled diff, not a full reset, so scroll position and selection survive. CodeMirror itself, and each individual language grammar, is dynamically imported the first time a snippet actually renders — a page with no `AiChatCodeSnippet` on it never downloads any of this.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@code` | `string` |  | The code to display/edit. The sole content source - see the class doc. |
| `@language` | `string` |  | Language used for syntax highlighting (an exact `@codemirror/language-data` name, or a common alias/extension - see `-code-snippet/language-utils.ts`). |
| `@editable` | `boolean` |  | Whether the snippet is an editable surface rather than a read-only display. |
| `@highlight` | `boolean` |  | Enables syntax highlighting (language detection/label-locking still runs either way). |
| `@defaultLanguage` | `string` |  | Fallback language used for empty editable content when nothing else resolves one. Defaults to `'javascript'`. |
| `@detectLanguage` | `boolean` |  | Show the detected language label in the header. When `false` (the default), only an explicit `@language` renders a label. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideCopyButton` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideHeader` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideLineNumbers` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideFold` | `boolean` |  | Hides the fold gutter, removing the ability to collapse/expand code blocks (drops the fold keymap too). |
| `@maxCollapsedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Max rows shown when collapsed. `0` (with `@maxExpandedNumberOfRows` also `0`) enables fill-container mode; `Infinity` grows with content instead of scrolling. Defaults to `15`. |
| `@maxExpandedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Max rows shown when expanded (`0` = unlimited). Defaults to `0`. |
| `@minCollapsedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Min rows shown when collapsed. Defaults to `3`. |
| `@minExpandedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Min rows shown when expanded. Defaults to `16`. |
| `@showLessText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@showMoreText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@copyButtonTooltipContent` | `string` |  |  |
| `@foldCollapseLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `@foldExpandLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabelEditable` | `string` |  | Aria-label for the editable surface. `{language}` is replaced with the detected/declared language once locked in. Defaults to `'Code editor'`. |
| `@ariaLabelReadOnly` | `string` |  | Aria-label for the read-only surface. `{language}` is replaced with the detected/declared language once locked in. Defaults to `'Code snippet'`. |
| `@getLineCountText` | `LineCountFormatter` |  | Formats the line-count label. Defaults to `${count} lines`. |
| `@actions` | `ToolbarAction[]` |  | Extra toolbar actions, rendered after the copy button (unless `@hideCopyButton`). |
| `@overflow` | `boolean` |  | Enables responsive overflow on the toolbar - see `Toolbar`'s own `@overflow`. |
| `@onChange` | `(content: string) => void` |  | Fires with the new content on every edit. Only meaningful with `@editable={{true}}` - a read-only snippet never changes its own doc. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

ai-chat-truncated-text · ./src/components/ai-chat/truncated-text.stories.gts
Info
No description found. Write a jsdoc comment such as /** Component description */.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-left" \| "top-start" \| "top-right" \| "top-end" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-end" \| "left-bottom" \| "left-end" \| "left-top" \| "left-start" \| "right-bottom" \| "right-end" \| "right-top" \| "right-start"` |  | Tooltip alignment when `@type` is `'tooltip'`. Defaults to `'top'`. |
| `@autoalign` | `boolean` |  | Auto-align the tooltip so it stays within the viewport. |
| `@collapseLabel` | `string` |  | Label for the collapse ("show less") button in `'expand'` mode. |
| `@expandLabel` | `string` |  | Label for the expand ("show more") button in `'expand'` mode. |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@lines` | `number` |  | Maximum number of lines to show before truncating. Defaults to `0` (no clamping). |
| `@type` | `"tooltip" \| "expand"` |  | How the full text is revealed once truncated: a `'tooltip'` on hover/focus, or an inline `'expand'`/collapse toggle. Defaults to `'tooltip'`. |
| `@value` | `string` |  | The string to truncate. Ignored if a default block is passed. |
| `@isLayered` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, renders the `'expand'` toggle button's layered background variant. Upstream derives this by sniffing for a `cds-layer` DOM ancestor at connect time; this port exposes it as a plain arg instead rather than reproducing that ancestry sniffing. |

## Blocks

- default block: Alternative to `@value` for rich/slotted content.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

AILabel

components-ailabel · ./src/components/ai-label.stories.gts
An AI label marks content that AI generated or influenced. Its button opens an explanation of how AI was used: put it in the yielded `Content`, with any buttons in `Actions`. Components such as Tag, TextArea, Dropdown and DatePickerInput take an AI label in their `<:decorator>` block, which yields an `AILabel` already sized for them.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@aiText` | `string` |  | The text in the label's button. Defaults to `AI`. |
| `@textLabel` | `string` |  | With `@kind="inline"`, text shown after `@aiText`, which then also names the button. |
| `@kind` | `"default" \| "inline"` |  | `default` is a small tag-like button; `inline` sits in running text. |
| `@size` | `AILabelSize` |  | Defaults to `xs`. Components that host an AI label pass their own. |
| `@align` | `ToggletipAlignment` |  | Where the label's content opens relative to its button. |
| `@defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Opens the content on first render. |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Read after `@aiText` to name the button. Defaults to `Show information`. |
| `@revertActive` | `boolean` |  | Shows a button that reverts AI-changed content, in place of the label, for when the user has edited it. |
| `@revertLabel` | `string` |  | Names the revert button. Defaults to `Revert to AI input`. |
| `@onRevertClick` | `() => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `Content`: component
    - `Actions`: component

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

AudioPlayer

ai-chat-audio-player · ./src/components/ai-chat/audio-player.stories.gts
`AudioPlayer` plays audio for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat). It supports native `<audio>` files (mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ...) and SoundCloud track URLs, auto-detected from `@source`. A source it doesn't recognize surfaces `@errorMessage` through the error state and `@onError` rather than failing silently.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@source` (required) | `string` |  | Audio source URL (required). |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Audio player'`. |
| `@playing` | `boolean` |  | Whether the audio should be playing. Only reacted to on later change - the initial value is applied via provider autoplay. |
| `@errorMessage` | `string` |  | Generic error message shown/reported regardless of the actual failure. Defaults to `'Failed to load audio'`. |
| `@loadingStatusMessage` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Audio player loading'`. |
| `@readyStatusMessage` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Audio player ready'`. |
| `@loadingLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Loading'`. |
| `@readyLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Ready'`. |
| `@errorLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Error'`. |
| `@onReady` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onPlay` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onPause` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onError` | `(detail: { message: string; }) => void` |  |  |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

import AudioPlayer from 'carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/audio-player';

BarChart

charts-barchart · ./src/components/charts/bar.stories.gts
A simple bar chart, rendered by `@carbon/charts`. It yields `Axis` (one each for `left` and `bottom`, both required), `TabularData` (one per data group, from `@values` plus `@keys` or `@dates`, or from `@data`), `ColorScale` (a color per group) and `ColorPairing` (a Carbon color pairing). Load `@carbon/charts/styles.css` alongside the Carbon styles.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@title` | `string` |  | The chart's title, rendered by |
| `@resizable` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@legendClickable` | `boolean` |  |  |

- default block

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

Button

components-button · ./src/components/button.stories.gts
Buttons are used to initialize an action. Pick the emphasis with `@type` (`primary`, `secondary` or `danger`), `@tertiary` or `@ghost`, and the size with `@size`. If `@onClick` returns a promise, the button disables itself and shows a loading indicator until the promise settles. A `danger` button asks for confirmation in a modal (with `@confirmText` as its body, or a custom `@confirmDialog`) before running `@onClick`; the modal renders into the `carbon.dialog-manager` service's destination element (`#carbon-components-dialog-id`), which the app has to provide.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@loading` | `boolean` |  | Will display a spinning Wheel inside the button |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@bubbles` | `boolean` |  | Pass `false` to cancel the click's default action, such as a `type="submit"` button submitting its form. The click still bubbles. |
| `@onClick` | `() => void \| Promise<unknown> \| null` |  |  |
| `@type` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "danger"` |  | Indicates the type of the button |
| `@primary` | `boolean` |  | Same as `@type="primary"`. |
| `@secondary` | `boolean` |  | Same as `@type="secondary"`. |
| `@danger` | `boolean` |  | Same as `@type="danger"`, including the confirmation dialog before `@onClick` runs. |
| `@confirmText` | `string` |  | If the action is dangerous, this text message will be shown in the dialog |
| `@confirmDialog` | `typeof ConfirmDialog` |  | Use this component as dialog |
| `@tertiary` | `boolean` |  | If the button is tertiary |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` |  | the button size |
| `@ghost` | `boolean` |  | If the button is a ghost button |
| `@label` | `string` |  |  |
| `@iconOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block

Carousel

ai-chat-carousel · ./src/components/ai-chat/carousel.stories.gts
`Carousel` is a view-stack carousel for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat). Each direct child passed to its default block becomes one view. Unlike the rest of this addon's AI Chat components, navigation, the change event and the `N / M` index readout aren't reimplemented here — they delegate directly to `@carbon/utilities`'s `initCarousel`, the same view-stack engine upstream itself uses.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@nextBtnText` | `string` |  | Tooltip/assistive text for the "next" button. |
| `@previousBtnText` | `string` |  | Tooltip/assistive text for the "previous" button. |
| `@onChange` | `(data: CarouselResponse) => void` |  | Called whenever the active view finishes transitioning. |

## Blocks

- default block: Each direct child rendered here becomes one carousel view (upstream's unnamed/"body" slot - its own JSDoc calls it `body`, but the actual implementation never names the slot, an upstream doc/code mismatch this port doesn't "fix", matching this addon's own precedent for upstream inconsistencies).

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

      <:body><div style="padding: 1rem;">{{card}}</div></:body>
    </AiChatCard>
  {{/each}}
</Carousel>

ChainOfThought

ai-chat-chain-of-thought · ./src/components/ai-chat/chain-of-thought.stories.gts
`ChainOfThought` and its yielded `ChainOfThoughtStep` render a collapsible list of tool-call-style steps for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat). The container's own `@open` toggles the whole panel; each step toggles independently and shows a status icon (success/failure/processing).
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel that wraps this chain of thought's steps is open. |
| `@controlled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, propagated to every yielded step as its own `@controlled`. |
| `@panelId` | `string` |  | ID applied to the content panel `<div>`. |
| `@onToggle` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called whenever `@open` changes after initial render, including externally-driven changes (not just user interaction) — mirrors upstream's `updated()`-driven `chain-of-thought-toggled` event. Passes just the new open state, not upstream's panel element, for consistency with this port's other `onToggle` callbacks (e.g. `ChainOfThoughtStep`). |

## Blocks

- default block: Renders one `<ChainOfThoughtStep>` per step. Yields the step component pre-bound with `@controlled`, mirroring `Layer`'s `WithBoundArgs` pattern for propagating a single arg down an arbitrary number of children.

ChainOfThoughtToggle

ai-chat-chain-of-thought-toggle · ./src/components/ai-chat/chain-of-thought-toggle.stories.gts
A standalone disclosure button for a `ChainOfThought` panel. Upstream keeps the two components DOM-decoupled (they only agree via `@panelId`/ `aria-controls`), so this port does too — wire `@onToggle` to whatever should happen, typically setting a `ChainOfThought`'s own `@open`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel this toggle controls is open. |
| `@openLabelText` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Hide chain of thought'`. |
| `@closedLabelText` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Show chain of thought'`. |
| `@panelId` | `string` |  | `aria-controls` target — typically a `ChainOfThought`'s `@panelId`. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onToggle` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new open state whenever the button is clicked. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLButtonElement`.

ChatHistory

ai-chat-chat-history · ./src/components/ai-chat/chat-history.stories.gts
`ChatHistory` is the entry-point shell for the chat history feature: a `header`/`toolbar`/`content` block, assembled from `ChatHistoryHeader`, `ChatHistoryToolbar`, `ChatHistoryContent` and `ChatHistoryPanel` (in turn yielding `ChatHistoryPanelItems`, `ChatHistoryPanelItem` and `ChatHistoryPanelMenu`). Renaming an item swaps it for a `ChatHistoryPanelItemInput`; deleting one shows a `ChatHistoryDeletePanel` overlay. `ChatHistorySearchItem` renders search results and `ChatHistoryLoading` the loading state. Each has its own stories under **AI Chat/Chat history**.
API description 
## Blocks

- `<:header>`: Typically a `ChatHistoryHeader`.
- `<:toolbar>`: Typically a `ChatHistoryToolbar`.
- `<:content>`: Typically a `ChatHistoryContent` wrapping a `ChatHistoryPanel` (or a `ChatHistoryLoading`).

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

ChatHistoryPanel

ai-chat-chat-history-panel · ./src/components/ai-chat/chat-history-panel.stories.gts
A `cds--side-nav`-styled panel listing chat history items, yielding `ChatHistoryPanelItems` pre-bound with `@showActions`. Typically rendered inside a `ChatHistoryContent`, itself inside `ChatHistory`'s `content` block - see **AI Chat/Chat history** for a fuller, interactive example.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@expanded` | `boolean` |  | Defaults to `true`. Upstream's `history-panel` always forces its underlying `CDSSideNav`'s `collapse-mode` to `'fixed'` (see its `connectedCallback`) - this port always renders in that fixed mode too, so `@expanded` only toggles between the "expanded"/"collapsed" CSS classes, never the hover/rail/responsive behavior a plain `CDSSideNav` would otherwise have. Those responsive modes aren't part of what `history-panel` itself exposes, so they aren't ported. |
| `@showActions` | `boolean` |  | `true` to always show every descendant `ChatHistoryPanelItem`'s overflow-actions menu, instead of only on hover/focus/selection. Propagated down to every yielded item. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `ChatHistoryPanelItems` (component)

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

ChatHistoryPanelItem

ai-chat-chat-history-panel-item · ./src/components/ai-chat/chat-history-panel-item.stories.gts
A single chat history entry: a selectable row with a name and an overflow-actions menu, or (when `@rename` is set) swapped for a `ChatHistoryPanelItemInput`. Usually obtained via `ChatHistoryPanelItems`'s or `ChatHistoryPanelMenu`'s yielded block param rather than imported directly - see **AI Chat/Chat history** for a fuller, interactive example wiring rename/delete together.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@selected` | `boolean` |  | `true` if this item is the currently-selected chat. |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Id of this chat history item, threaded through to every callback. |
| `@name` | `string` |  |  |
| `@rename` | `boolean` |  | `true` to enter rename mode (swaps to a `ChatHistoryPanelItemInput`). Upstream's own `history-panel-item.ts` mutates its own `rename` field back to `false` directly once a rename is saved/canceled, rather than treating it as a value the host exclusively owns (a looser convention common in plain web components, not a strict controlled/uncontrolled split) - this port matches that: a local save/cancel always exits rename mode immediately (without waiting for `@rename` to change), while `@onRenameSave`/`@onRenameCancel` still fire so a host can keep its own state in sync. `@rename` itself is mirrored in both directions by `watchRename` below, so a host resetting `@rename` back to `false` (e.g. because it switched to renaming a *different* item) also closes this item's rename UI. |
| `@actions` | `ChatHistoryItemAction[]` |  |  |
| `@overflowMenuLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Options'`. |
| `@showActions` | `boolean` |  | `true` to always show the overflow-actions menu (usually bound from `ChatHistoryPanel`/`ChatHistoryPanelItems`). |
| `@renameInvalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@renameInvalidMessage` | `string` |  |  |
| `@parentMenuExpanded` | `boolean` |  | `true` if this item's parent `ChatHistoryPanelMenu` group is expanded (or if it has no parent group). Controls whether the overflow menu is even reachable while collapsed - bound down from `ChatHistoryPanelMenu`. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@onSelect` | `(detail: { itemId?: string \| undefined; itemName?: string \| undefined; }) => void` |  |  |
| `@onRenameChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@onRenameCancel` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onRenameSave` | `(newName: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@onMenuAction` | `(detail: { action?: string \| undefined; itemId?: string \| undefined; itemName?: string \| undefined; }) => void` |  | Upstream's own `Action` type declares a per-action `onClick`, but its actual render() wires every `cds-overflow-menu-item` to one shared handler that dispatches a single `history-item-menu-action` event with the action's text - `action.onClick` is never actually invoked (matches this port's "match behavior over intent" principle elsewhere). This port omits `onClick` from `ChatHistoryItemAction` entirely rather than accepting-and-ignoring it, and exposes the real behavior as a single `@onMenuAction` callback instead. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLLIElement`.
Imports

    @onMenuAction={{@onMenuAction}}

A collapsible group of `ChatHistoryPanelItem`s (e.g. "Today", "Yesterday"), rendered inside a `ChatHistoryPanelItems`. Uncontrolled by default (starts expanded, toggles itself on click); pass `@expanded` + `@onToggle` together for a fully controlled group.

| `@showActions` | `boolean` |  | Propagated down to every yielded `ChatHistoryPanelItem`. |

ChatShell

ai-chat-chat-shell · ./src/components/ai-chat/chat-shell.stories.gts
`ChatShell` is the layout shell for a [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat) window — header, message history, input, and optional history/workspace side panels. Content is supplied entirely through named blocks; `ChatShell` itself owns no conversation state. `@showHistory`/`@showWorkspace` are always-controlled booleans — there is no uncontrolled/default-open variant, matching upstream's own API. The `input` block is entirely caller-supplied too — `ChatShell` doesn't own a text field or send button. The **With prompt line** story composes `PromptLineShell` + `PromptLine` (upstream's own separate `prompt-line` component) into it.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@aiEnabled` | `boolean` |  | Enables AI-specific theming for the chat shell. |
| `@showFrame` | `boolean` |  | Shows a frame border around the chat shell. |
| `@cornerAll` | `CornerStyle` |  | Sets the corner style for all corners. Individual `@cornerStartStart` / `@cornerStartEnd` / `@cornerEndStart` / `@cornerEndEnd` args override this value. Defaults to `'square'`. Upstream renders each corner independently via a per-instance dynamic stylesheet (`CornerManager`). This port only distinguishes "at least one corner is round" vs. "all square" (a single `.rounded` modifier class) — genuinely mixed round/square corners on one shell aren't yet supported. |
| `@cornerStartStart` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the start-start corner (top-left in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@cornerStartEnd` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the start-end corner (top-right in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@cornerEndStart` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the end-start corner (bottom-left in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@cornerEndEnd` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the end-end corner (bottom-right in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@showHistory` | `boolean` |  | Shows the history panel. Always-controlled boolean — matches upstream's `show-history` attribute, which has no `default-show-history` counterpart and no change event, so there's no uncontrolled path to offer (see AGENTS.md §3). |
| `@showWorkspace` | `boolean` |  | Shows the workspace panel. Always-controlled, same shape as `@showHistory`. |
| `@workspaceLocation` | `StartOrEnd` |  | Location of the workspace panel. Defaults to `'start'`. |
| `@historyLocation` | `StartOrEnd` |  | Location of the history panel. Defaults to `'start'`. |
| `@workspaceAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the workspace region. |
| `@historyAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the history region. |
| `@messagesAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the messages region. |
| `@panelOpenedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when a (non-workspace) panel opens. Accepted for API parity; nothing in this port dispatches the panel open/close events upstream keys this announcement off, since the `panels` block's content is entirely up to the caller here (see class doc). |
| `@panelClosedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when a (non-workspace) panel closes. See `@panelOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when the workspace opens. Accepted for API parity; not yet wired to an actual screen-reader announcement in this port (see class doc). |
| `@workspaceClosedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when the workspace closes. See `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@historyShownAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when history becomes visible. See `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@historyHiddenAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when history becomes hidden. See `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@contentMaxWidth` | `boolean` |  | Constrains the input/messages column to a maximum width. When `false`, those slots extend to the full container width. |

## Blocks

- `<:header>`: Upstream `header` slot.
- `<:headerAfter>`: Upstream `header-after` slot.
- `<:footer>`: Upstream `footer` slot.
- `<:inputBefore>`: Upstream `input-before` slot.
- `<:input>`: Upstream `input` slot.
- `<:inputAfter>`: Upstream `input-after` slot.
- `<:messages>`: Upstream `messages` slot — the conversation itself.
- `<:history>`: Upstream `history` slot. Only rendered when `@showHistory` is true.
- `<:workspace>`: Upstream `workspace` slot. Only rendered when `@showWorkspace` is true.
- `<:panels>`: Upstream `panels` slot, for arbitrary caller-managed overlay panels.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import ChatShell from 'carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/chat-shell';

Checkbox

components-checkbox · ./src/components/checkbox.stories.gts
Checkboxes are used when there are multiple items to select in a list. Users can select zero, one, or any number of items. Checkbox is controlled: pass `@checked` and update it from `@onChange`, which receives the new checked state.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@name` | `string` |  |  |
| `@readonly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@indeterminate` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@checked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| `@state` | `object` |  |  |
| `@label` | `string` |  |  |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Visually hide the label, keeping it as the checkbox's accessible name (as Carbon React's `hideLabel`). |

- default block
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown after the label. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it; with `@kind="inline"`, also pass `@size="md"`.

CodeSnippet

components-codesnippet · ./src/components/code-snippet.stories.gts
Code snippets are strings or small blocks of reusable code that can be copied and inserted in a code file. Pass the code as the block. `@type` picks the variant: `default` (a single line), `multiline` (collapsed to 240px with a "Show more" toggle) or `inline` (a copy button that shows the code inline in running text).
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@type` (required) | `"default" \| "inline" \| "multiline"` |  |  |

DataTable

components-datatable-basic · ./src/components/data-table/basic.stories.gts
Data tables are used to organize and display data efficiently. The data table component allows for customization with additional functionality, as needed by your product’s users. `DataTable` yields its building blocks already wired to the table: `Toolbar` (with `Content` and the batch-action bar `Actions`), `SearchInput`, `Table`, `Header`, `EachBodyRows` (yielding a `Row` per item), `Column`, `Menu` and `Pagination`. Every `<td>` is automatically linked to its column's `<th>` via the `headers` attribute for screen-reader users.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@onSelectionChange` | `(items: T[]) => void` |  |  |
| `@registerState` | `(state: State<T>) => void` |  |  |
| `@search` | `() => Promise<boolean>` |  |  |
| `@state` | `State<T>` |  |  |
| `@items` (required) | `T[]` |  |  |
| `@isLoading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@title` | `string` |  |  |
| `@description` | `string` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `Toolbar`: component
    - `SearchInput`: component
    - `Pagination`: component
    - `Table`: component
    - `EachBodyRows`: component
    - `Column`: component
    - `Menu`: component
    - `Header`: component

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import DataTable from 'carbon-components-ember/components/data-table';
Default story ok 
<DataTable
  @title="DataTable"
  @description="With toolbar"
  @isLoading={{@isLoading}}
  @items={{ROWS}}
  as |table|
>
  <table.Toolbar as |toolbar|>
    <toolbar.Content>
      <table.SearchInput @expandable={{true}} />
    </toolbar.Content>
  </table.Toolbar>
  <table.Table @size="lg" @useZebraStyles={{false}}>
    <table.Header @headers={{HEADERS_WITH_MENU}} />
    <table.EachBodyRows as |row|>
      <row.Row>
        <Cells @Column={{table.Column}} @item={{row.item}} />
        <table.Menu as |Item|>
          <Item @itemText="Edit" />
        </table.Menu>
      </row.Row>
    </table.EachBodyRows>
  </table.Table>
  <table.Pagination />
</DataTable>

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

| `@registerState` | `(state: State<T>) => void` |  |  |
| `@search` | `() => Promise<boolean>` |  |  |
| `@state` | `State<T>` |  |  |
| `@items` (required) | `T[]` |  |  |
| `@isLoading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@title` | `string` |  |  |
| `@description` | `string` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block

DataTableSkeleton

components-datatable-skeleton · ./src/components/data-table/skeleton.stories.gts
A loading placeholder for a `DataTable`, for before there is any data to give it. Pass it the headers you will give the table, and it shows a column for each. A `DataTable` that already has its data can show `@isLoading` instead.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@columnCount` | `number` |  | Defaults to one column per header, or 5 without `@headers`. |
| `@headers` | `(Header \| null \| undefined)[]` |  | Column headings to show in place of placeholders, in the shape `DataTable`'s `Header` takes. |
| `@rowCount` | `number` |  | Defaults to 5. |
| `@showHeader` | `boolean` |  | Shows placeholders for the title and description. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@showToolbar` | `boolean` |  | Shows a placeholder toolbar. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs" \| "xl"` |  | Row height. Defaults to `lg`. |
| `@zebra` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLTableElement`.
Imports 
import DataTableSkeleton from 'carbon-components-ember/components/data-table-skeleton';
Skeleton story ok 
<div style="width: 800px">
  <DataTableSkeleton
    @headers={{HEADERS}}
    @columnCount={{@columnCount}}
    @rowCount={{5}}
    @showHeader={{true}}
    @showToolbar={{true}}
    @size="lg"
    @zebra={{false}}
    aria-label="sample table"
  />
</div>
Loading story ok
`@isLoading` puts a `DataTable`, its search and its pagination into their loading state.
<DataTable
  @title="DataTable"
  @description="With toolbar"
  @isLoading={{true}}
  @items={{ROWS}}
  as |table|
>
  <table.Toolbar as |toolbar|>
    <toolbar.Content>
      <table.SearchInput @expandable={{true}} />
    </toolbar.Content>
  </table.Toolbar>
  <table.Table>
    <table.Header @headers={{HEADERS_WITH_MENU}} />
    <table.EachBodyRows as |row|>
      <row.Row>
        <Cells @Column={{table.Column}} @item={{row.item}} />
        <table.Menu as |Item|>
          <Item @itemText="Edit" />
        </table.Menu>
      </row.Row>
    </table.EachBodyRows>
  </table.Table>
  <table.Pagination />
</DataTable>

DatePicker

components-datepicker · ./src/components/date-picker.stories.gts
DatePicker lets a user pick a date, or a range of dates, from a calendar dropdown, or type one into a plain field. It wraps [flatpickr](https://flatpickr.js.org/) for the calendar and composes one or two `DatePickerInput` fields, yielded from the block, to render the field(s) themselves. The calendar dropdown renders inside `DatePicker`'s own container by default, so it stays inside whatever root - shadow or document - the picker itself renders into. Pass a different element as `@appendTo` to redirect it elsewhere instead, e.g. to escape an `overflow: hidden` ancestor.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@datePickerType` | `DatePickerType` |  | `simple` renders a plain text field with no calendar. `single` and `range` render a calendar dropdown (backed by flatpickr), for one date or two (start/end) respectively. |
| `@dateFormat` | `string` |  | A flatpickr format string controlling how dates are displayed and parsed. |
| `@value` | `DatePickerValue` |  | The date (or, for `range`, the `[start, end]` dates) to seed the field(s) with. Controlled: later changes to `@value` are re-synced onto the field(s) (via the live flatpickr instance for `single`/`range`, or written directly to the input for `simple`) - see `syncValue`. Accepts anything flatpickr's own `defaultDate`/`setDate` accept (a `Date`, a date string, a timestamp, or - for `range` - an array of two). |
| `@minDate` | `DateOption` |  | The minimum selectable date. |
| `@maxDate` | `DateOption` |  | The maximum selectable date. |
| `@allowInput` | `boolean` |  | Flatpickr prop passthrough: whether the field(s) can be edited by typing directly, in addition to picking from the calendar. |
| `@closeOnSelect` | `boolean` |  | Whether the calendar dropdown closes as soon as a date is picked. |
| `@appendTo` | `HTMLElement` |  | The DOM node flatpickr's calendar dropdown is appended into. Defaults to the picker's own container element, so the calendar always lands in the same root (shadow or document) the picker itself renders into - flatpickr's own default of `document.body` would otherwise make the calendar escape a shadow root, where your styles don't reach it. Pass an explicit node to redirect it elsewhere instead (e.g. to escape a `overflow: hidden` ancestor). |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Whether the field(s) are read-only. A read-only picker has no calendar and cannot be typed into. |
| `@short` | `boolean` |  | Renders the compact/short variant. |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `DatePickerChangeHandler` |  | Called whenever the selection changes. |
| `@onOpen` | `DatePickerChangeHandler` |  | Called when the calendar dropdown opens. |
| `@onClose` | `DatePickerChangeHandler` |  | Called when the calendar dropdown closes. |

## Blocks

- default block: Yields `DatePickerInput`, pre-bound to this picker's `@datePickerType` and `@readOnly`. Render one for `simple`/`single`, two (start, then end) for `range`.
  - yields `DatePickerInput` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

  @datePickerType="single"

  @value={{@value}}
  @minDate={{@minDate}}

  @allowInput={{@allowInput}}

components-datepicker-datepickerinput · ./src/components/date-picker-input.stories.gts
The text `<input>` rendered for each field of a `DatePicker`: one for a `single` or `simple` picker, two (start and end) for a `range` picker. Render it through the `DatePicker` block, which yields it already wired to the picker; pass `@value` to the `DatePicker`, not to the input.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | The id of the `<input>`. Also used to associate the label with the field. Auto-generated when omitted. |
| `@labelText` (required) | `string` |  | The text read by assistive technology and (unless `@hideLabel` is set) rendered above the field. |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Visually hide the label, while still keeping it available to assistive technology. |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  | Placeholder text shown in the field when it is empty. |
| `@pattern` | `string` |  | A regular expression pattern the input's value must match. |
| `@type` | `string` |  | The `<input>` element's `type` attribute. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the field. |
| `@datePickerType` | `"single" \| "simple" \| "range"` |  | Set by the parent `DatePicker` (`simple` renders no calendar icon unless `@invalid`/`@warn` is set). |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether or not the input should be disabled. |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Whether the field is read-only. Set by the parent `DatePicker` when it is read-only. |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the value is invalid. |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the value is invalid. |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently in warning state. |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the control is in warning state. |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  | Provide text that is used alongside the control label for additional help. |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Called whenever the raw `<input>` fires a `change` event. `DatePicker` drives the actual value through flatpickr directly on the DOM node; this is for consumers that want the raw text as the user types it. |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Called when the field is clicked. |

## Blocks

- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import DatePickerInput from 'carbon-components-ember/components/date-picker-input';
Default story ok 
<DatePicker
  @datePickerType="single"
  @readOnly={{@readOnly}}
  as |Input|
>
  <Input
    @id={{@id}}
    @labelText="Date Picker label"
    @hideLabel={{false}}
    @placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    @pattern={{@pattern}}
    @type={{@type}}
    @size={{@size}}
    @disabled={{false}}
    @invalid={{false}}
    @invalidText="A valid value is required"
    @warn={{false}}
    @warnText="Warning message that is really long can wrap to more lines"
    @helperText="Optional helper text"
    @onChange={{@onChange}}
    @onClick={{@onClick}}
  />
</DatePicker>

Dropdown

components-dropdown · ./src/components/dropdown.stories.gts
`Dropdown` is a single-select field that opens a listbox of items on click. It renders Carbon's `ListBox` markup directly - the menu is a plain descendant of the field, positioned with Carbon's own CSS - and manages its own open/highlight state internally. Items can be any value: `@itemToString` turns one into its label (the default is `String(item)`), or a block can render each item.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | The id of the underlying field button. Also used to derive the ids of the label and menu, so the ARIA wiring between them stays consistent. Auto-generated when omitted. |
| `@items` (required) | `T[]` |  | The list of items to choose from. |
| `@titleText` (required) | `string` |  | The field's label, rendered above the control. |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | Placeholder text shown in the field when nothing is selected. |
| `@itemToString` | `(item: T) => string` |  | Convert an item to display text. Used both for the field button's `title` attribute and, when no item block is supplied, as the default rendering of each menu item. Defaults to reading a `label` property off the item, falling back to an empty string. |
| `@selectedItem` | `NonNullable<T>` |  | The currently selected item (controlled). Wins over internal state whenever it is defined. |
| `@initialSelectedItem` | `NonNullable<T>` |  | Seeds the initially selected item for the uncontrolled case. |
| `@onChange` | `(data: { selectedItem: T \| null; }) => void` |  | Called whenever the selection changes, with the newly selected item. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the control should be disabled, or not. |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the control should be read-only. A read-only field button remains focusable but cannot be opened or changed. |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the currently selected value is invalid. |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the value is invalid. |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently in warning state. |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the control is in warning state. |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  | Provide text that is used alongside the control label for additional help. |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Visually hide the label, while still keeping it available to assistive technology. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the Dropdown. |
| `@type` | `"default" \| "inline"` |  | `default` renders the standalone field; `inline` lays the field out next to its label (via flex layout classes) and suppresses the helper text row. The label itself is always rendered - use `@hideLabel` to visually hide it. |
| `@direction` | `"top" \| "bottom"` |  | The direction the menu should open in. |

## Blocks

- default block: Customize how each item renders in the menu. Falls back to `itemToString(item)` when no block is supplied. The field button's own text always uses `itemToString`, matching React's default behaviour when `renderSelectedItem` is not passed.
  - yields `item` (`T`)
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

  @hideLabel={{@hideLabel}}
  @size={{@size}}
  @type={{@type}}
  @direction={{@direction}}
  @disabled={{@disabled}}

FeedbackButtons

ai-chat-feedback-buttons · ./src/components/ai-chat/feedback-buttons.stories.gts
`FeedbackButtons` renders a thumbs-up / thumbs-down pair used to collect quick feedback on a chat response, each optionally wired to its own details panel (typically a `Feedback`) via `aria-controls` (`@panelId` + `-feedback-positive`/`-feedback-negative`).
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@isPositiveOpen` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isNegativeOpen` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isPositiveSelected` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isNegativeSelected` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hasPositiveDetails` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hasNegativeDetails` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isPositiveDisabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isNegativeDisabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@positiveLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Good response'`. |
| `@negativeLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Bad response'`. |
| `@panelId` | `string` |  | ID prefix used to build `aria-controls` for each button's own details panel. |
| `@onClick` | `(isPositive: boolean) => void` |  | Called with `true` for the thumbs-up button, `false` for thumbs-down. |

With Details Panel story ok 
<div style="padding: 2rem;">
  <p style="margin-bottom: 1rem;">
    Both buttons open details panels for collecting more information. Try
    clicking the thumbs up or thumbs down buttons to provide feedback.
  </p>
  <FeedbackButtons
    @hasPositiveDetails={{@hasPositiveDetails}}
    @hasNegativeDetails={{@hasNegativeDetails}}
    @isPositiveOpen={{state.positiveOpen}}
    @isNegativeOpen={{state.negativeOpen}}
    @isPositiveSelected={{state.positiveSelected}}
    @isNegativeSelected={{state.negativeSelected}}
    @isPositiveDisabled={{state.positiveDisabled}}
    @isNegativeDisabled={{state.negativeDisabled}}
    @positiveLabel="I like this response"
    @negativeLabel="I dislike this response"
    @panelId={{panelId}}
    @onClick={{state.toggle}}
  />
  <div style="margin-block-start: 1rem; max-inline-size: 26rem;">
    {{#if args.hasPositiveDetails}}
      <Feedback
        @id={{positivePanelId}}
        @isOpen={{state.positiveOpen}}
        @isReadonly={{state.submitted}}
        @categories={{POSITIVE_CATEGORIES}}
        @initialValues={{state.positiveInitialValues}}
        @title="Additional feedback"
        @body="Why did you choose this rating?"
        @placeholder="Add a comment"
        @primaryLabel="Submit"
        @showBody={{true}}
        @showTextArea={{true}}
        @onClose={{state.closePositive}}
        @onSubmit={{state.submitPositive}}
      />
    {{/if}}
    {{#if args.hasNegativeDetails}}
      <Feedback
        @id={{negativePanelId}}
        @isOpen={{state.negativeOpen}}
        @isReadonly={{state.submitted}}
        @categories={{NEGATIVE_CATEGORIES}}
        @initialValues={{state.negativeInitialValues}}
        @title="Additional feedback"
        @body="Why did you choose this rating?"
        @placeholder="Add a comment"
        @primaryLabel="Submit"
        @showBody={{true}}
        @showTextArea={{true}}
        @onClose={{state.closeNegative}}
        @onSubmit={{state.submitNegative}}
      />
    {{/if}}
  </div>
  {{#if state.lastSubmission}}
    <p
      class="feedback-demo-note"
      style="margin-block-start: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.875rem;"
    >
      Last submission:
      <strong>
        {{if state.lastSubmission.isPositive "Positive" "Negative"}}
      </strong>
      {{#if state.lastSubmission.text}}
        —
        {{state.lastSubmission.text}}
      {{/if}}
    </p>
  {{/if}}
</div>

FileUploader

components-fileuploader · ./src/components/file-uploader.stories.gts
`FileUploader` lets a user upload one or more files via a button that opens the native file picker, showing every selected file with the same `@filenameStatus`. It's the simple case; for a real upload flow — where files progress through their own `uploading` → `complete`/`edit` states independently, and users can drag and drop files onto the page — compose `FileUploaderDropContainer` and `FileUploaderItem` directly (see the drag-and-drop example applications). `FileUploader` yields a `clearFiles` action that resets the selected-file list, e.g. once a caller has finished uploading every file — it's the only supported way to reset the picker without destroying/recreating the component.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@accept` | `string[]` |  | Specify the types of files that this input should be able to receive |
| `@buttonKind` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "ghost" \| "danger" \| "danger--primary" \| "danger--ghost" \| "danger--tertiary"` |  | Specify the type of the underlying `FileUploaderButton` |
| `@buttonLabel` | `string` |  | Provide the label text read by screen readers for the upload button |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether file input is disabled |
| `@filenameStatus` (required) | `"complete" \| "edit" \| "uploading"` |  | Specify the status applied to every selected file |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Provide a description for the status icon, read by screen readers |
| `@labelDescription` | `string` |  | Specify the description text of this FileUploader |
| `@labelTitle` | `string` |  | Specify the title text of this FileUploader |
| `@maxFileSize` | `number` |  | Maximum file size allowed in bytes. Files larger than this are marked invalid |
| `@multiple` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the component should accept multiple files to upload |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Provide a name for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@onAddFiles` | `(event: Event, data: { addedFiles: FileUploaderAddedFile[]; }) => void` |  | Called after files are added, before they're marked invalid/filtered |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event, data: FileUploaderChangeData) => void` |  | Called each time the selected-file list changes |
| `@onClick` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Called each time a selected file's status icon is activated |
| `@onDelete` | `(event: Event, data: { deletedFile: FileUploaderFileItem; remainingFiles: FileUploaderFileItem[]; }) => void` |  | Called when a selected file is removed (only reachable when `@filenameStatus` is `'edit'`) |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "small" \| "field"` |  | Specify the size of the FileUploaderButton, from a list of available sizes |

## Blocks

- default block: Yields a `clearFiles`-style action that resets the selected-file list, e.g. after a successful upload
  - yields `clearFiles` (`() => void`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import FileUploader from 'carbon-components-ember/components/file-uploader';
Default story ok 
<div class="cds--file__container">
  <FileUploader
    @accept={{@accept}}
    @buttonKind={{@buttonKind}}
    @buttonLabel={{@buttonLabel}}
    @disabled={{@disabled}}
    @filenameStatus={{if args.filenameStatus args.filenameStatus "edit"}}
    @iconDescription={{@iconDescription}}
    @labelDescription={{@labelDescription}}
    @labelTitle={{@labelTitle}}
    @maxFileSize={{@maxFileSize}}
    @multiple={{@multiple}}
    @name={{@name}}
    @size={{@size}}
    @onAddFiles={{@onAddFiles}}
    @onChange={{@onChange}}
    @onClick={{@onClick}}
    @onDelete={{@onDelete}}
  />
</div>

FileUploaderButton

components-fileuploader-fileuploaderbutton · ./src/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-button.stories.gts
A button that opens the native file picker for a hidden `<input type="file">`, and then shows the picked file name (or the number of files) as its label unless `@disableLabelChanges` is set. `FileUploader` renders one; it can also be used on its own as the minimal button-triggered (non-drag-and-drop) upload pattern.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@accept` | `string[]` |  | Specify the types of files that this input should be able to receive |
| `@buttonKind` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "ghost" \| "danger" \| "danger--primary" \| "danger--ghost" \| "danger--tertiary"` |  | Specify the type of underlying button |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether file input is disabled |
| `@disableLabelChanges` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether you want to disable any updates to the button's label |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Provide a unique id for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  | Provide the label text to be read by screen readers when interacting with this control |
| `@multiple` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the component should accept multiple files to upload |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Provide a name for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Called each time the `<input>` value changes |
| `@onButtonInsert` | `(element: HTMLButtonElement) => void` |  | Called with the underlying `<button>` element once it's inserted, so a caller can drive it imperatively (e.g. restoring focus) |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "small" \| "field"` |  | Specify the size of the FileUploaderButton, from a list of available sizes |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLButtonElement`.
Imports 
import FileUploaderButton from 'carbon-components-ember/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-button';
Default story ok 
<FileUploaderButton
  @labelText="Add file"
  @multiple={{false}}
  @disabled={{false}}
  @disableLabelChanges={{false}}
  @buttonKind="primary"
  @size="md"
/>

FileUploaderDropContainer

components-fileuploader-fileuploaderdropcontainer · ./src/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-drop-container.stories.gts
A drop target for files, with a hidden file picker as the click/keyboard fallback. It calls `@onAddFiles` with the added files (each marked `invalidFileType` when it doesn’t match `@accept` or exceeds `@maxFileSize`), but doesn’t list them: render a `FileUploaderItem` per file next to it, so each file’s status can progress on its own. See the drag-and-drop example applications on the `FileUploader` page.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@accept` | `string[]` |  | Specify the types of files that this input should be able to receive |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether file input is disabled |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Provide a unique id for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  | Provide the label text to be read by screen readers when interacting with this control |
| `@maxFileSize` | `number` |  | Maximum file size allowed in bytes. Files larger than this are marked invalid |
| `@multiple` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the component should accept multiple files to upload |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Provide a name for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@onAddFiles` | `(event: Event, data: { addedFiles: FileUploaderAddedFile[]; }) => void` |  | Called after files are added, either by drop or by the file picker |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Called each time the drop area is clicked |
| `@pattern` | `string` |  | Provide a custom regex pattern used to extract a file's extension |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import FileUploaderDropContainer from 'carbon-components-ember/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-drop-container';
Default story ok 
<FileUploaderDropContainer
  @disabled={{false}}
  @labelText="Drag and drop files here or click to upload"
  @multiple={{true}}
  @name=""
/>

FileUploaderItem

components-fileuploader-fileuploaderitem · ./src/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-item.stories.gts
One selected file in a `FileUploader`: its name plus a status icon that follows `@status` (`uploading`, `complete`, or `edit`, which shows a delete button that calls `@onDelete` with the item’s `@uuid`). `@invalid` shows `@errorSubject`/`@errorBody` below it. Render one per file next to a `FileUploaderDropContainer` to build a drag-and-drop upload flow.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the file uploader item is disabled |
| `@errorBody` | `string` |  | Error message body for an invalid file upload |
| `@errorSubject` | `string` |  | Error message subject for an invalid file upload |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Description of the status icon (read by assistive technology) |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the currently uploaded file is invalid |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Name of the uploaded file |
| `@onDelete` | `(event: Event, data: { uuid: string; }) => void` |  | Called after the item is removed, with the item's `uuid` |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the item, from a list of available sizes |
| `@status` | `"complete" \| "edit" \| "uploading"` |  | Status of the file upload |
| `@uuid` | `string` |  | Unique identifier for the file, generated when omitted |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLSpanElement`.
Imports 
import FileUploaderItem from 'carbon-components-ember/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-item';

no API description
elements-flexgrid · ./src/components/grid/row.stories.gts
The Flexbox flavour of the 2x Grid: a grid renders one or more `Row`s, and each `Row` renders one or more `Column`s. `FlexGrid` is an always-flexbox alias of `Grid` (whose default `@mode` is `flexbox` anyway), for parity with Carbon React. See *Elements/Grid* for the column span shorthand and the CSS Grid.

FluidTextInput

components-fluid-components-fluidtextinput · ./src/components/fluid-text-input.stories.gts
FluidTextInput is a text input variant with fluid styling - a full-width bottom divider and inline validation message, intended for use in fluid forms. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled field, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it. `@isPassword` masks the value and adds a visibility toggle. The `labelText` block replaces `@labelText` when the label needs markup.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@value` | `string` |  |  |
| `@defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@enableCounter` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@maxCount` | `number` |  |  |
| `@isPassword` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@showPasswordLabel` | `string` |  |  |

Grid

elements-grid · ./src/components/grid.stories.gts
The 2x Grid is a flexible, 16-column grid system that can be used to build custom layouts. Carbon ships two layout engines for it, and `Grid` renders either one: - **Flexbox grid** (the default, `@mode="flexbox"`) — a `Grid` renders one or more `GridRow`s, and each `GridRow` renders one or more `GridColumn`s. See *Elements/FlexGrid*. - **CSS Grid** (`@mode="css-grid"`, these stories) — there are no rows; columns are direct children of the `Grid`. This mode additionally supports subgrids, percentage spans, and explicit `start`/`end` placement. `Grid` yields `Grid`, `Column`, `Row` and `ColumnHang` components that are already bound to the surrounding grid's mode, so the mode is only picked once. ### Column span shorthand `GridColumn` accepts a value for each breakpoint (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xlg`, `max`): - `true` — the column takes up an equal share of the remaining space - a `number` — the column spans that many columns - an object like `{{hash span=4 offset=2}}` — the column spans `span` columns and is offset by `offset` columns In `css-grid` mode a column additionally accepts a percentage (`'25%'`, `'50%'`, `'75%'`, `'100%'`) and `start`/`end` grid lines.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@align` | `GridAlign` |  | Specify grid alignment. Default is center. Only applies when `mode` is `css-grid`. |
| `@condensed` | `boolean` |  | Collapse the gutter to 1px. Useful for fluid layouts. Rows have 1px of margin between them to match gutter. |
| `@fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Remove the default max width that the grid has set |
| `@mode` | `GridMode` | `'flexbox'` | Which layout engine to use. `flexbox` renders `cds--grid`/`cds--row`/ `cds--col-*`, `css-grid` renders `cds--css-grid`/`cds--css-grid-column`. |
| `@narrow` | `boolean` |  | Container hangs 16px into the gutter. Useful for typographic alignment with and without containers. |
| `@subgrid` | `boolean` |  | Render as a subgrid of a surrounding CSS Grid instead of as a new grid. Set automatically for the `Grid` yielded from another `Grid`. |
| `@withRowGap` | `boolean` |  | Add a row gap to the grid that matches the current gutter size. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `grid` (`GridBlock`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

`@align` positions the grid within its container. It defaults to `center` and only applies in `css-grid` mode. `@align` only has room to move the grid once its container is wider than the grid’s own max width, so the examples are placed in an artificially wide, dashed-outline container that’s wider than the grid itself.

GridColumn

elements-grid-gridcolumn · ./src/components/grid/column.stories.gts
A column of the 2x Grid. Render the `Column` yielded by `Grid` (or `GridSettings`), which already has the grid's `@mode`: in the CSS Grid it's a direct child of the `Grid`, in the Flexbox grid it goes inside a `GridRow`. Each breakpoint arg (`@sm`, `@md`, `@lg`, `@xlg`, `@max`) takes `true` (an equal share of the remaining space), a number of columns, or an object like `{{hash span=4 offset=2}}`. In `css-grid` mode a column also takes a percentage (`'25%'` ... `'100%'`), `start`/`end` grid lines, and a breakpoint-independent `@span`. See *Elements/Grid* for examples.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@mode` | `GridMode` | `'flexbox'` | Which grid engine the surrounding `Grid` uses. Normally inherited by invoking the `Column` yielded from `Grid`, but can be set explicitly when a column is rendered on its own. |
| `@sm` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `sm` breakpoint (up to 671px). This breakpoint supports 4 columns by default. |
| `@md` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `md` breakpoint (up to 1055px). This breakpoint supports 8 columns by default. |
| `@lg` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `lg` breakpoint (up to 1311px). This breakpoint supports 16 columns by default. |
| `@xlg` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `xlg` breakpoint (up to 1583px). This breakpoint supports 16 columns by default. |
| `@max` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `max` breakpoint. This breakpoint supports 16 columns by default. |
| `@span` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify a constant column span, start, or end value that does not change based on breakpoint. Only applies in `css-grid` mode. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import GridColumn from 'carbon-components-ember/components/grid/column';
Default story ok 
<Grid @mode="css-grid" as |g|>
  {{#if (isFlexbox args.mode)}}
    <g.Row><Columns @args={{args}} /></g.Row>
  {{else}}
    <Columns @args={{args}} />
  {{/if}}
</Grid>

elements-grid-gridrow · ./src/components/grid/grid-row.stories.gts
A row of the Flexbox grid: render it (the `Row` yielded by `Grid`) inside a flexbox `Grid` or `FlexGrid`, and the columns inside it. The CSS Grid has no rows. `@condensed` and `@narrow` change the gutter of a single row. See *Elements/FlexGrid* for examples.

| `@narrow` | `boolean` |  | Specify a single row as narrow. The container will hang 16px into the gutter. |

Icon

components-icon · ./src/components/icon.stories.gts
`Icon` renders a Carbon SVG icon. Use the generated icon components from `carbon-components-ember/icons` (e.g. `<Bookmark @size={{16}} />`), which load the SVG for the requested size on demand, or register an SVG from `@carbon/icons` with `registerIcon(name, svg)` and render it with `<Icon @icon="name" />`. Passing `@onClick` renders the icon inside a ghost button and shows a loading state while the (optionally async) handler runs.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@loading` | `boolean` |  | Indicates if the icon is in loading state |
| `@info` | `boolean` |  | Indicates if the icon is informative |
| `@danger` | `boolean` |  | Indicates if the action is dangerous, showing a confirmation dialog before calling `onClick` |
| `@confirmText` | `string` |  | If the action is dangerous, this text message will be shown in the dialog |
| `@confirmDialog` | `string` |  | Use this component as dialog |
| `@icon` | `string \| IconType` |  | Use this icon to display |
| `@iconSvg` | `TrustedHTML` |  | Use this icon svg to display, must be a htmlSafe string |
| `@size` | `string \| number` |  | Size of icon |
| `@onClick` | `() => void \| Promise<never>` |  | action to trigger on click |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Names the `@onClick` button for assistive technology (the icon itself is decorative). Required whenever `@onClick` is passed. |
| `@btnStyle` | `string` |  | button style |
| `@btnClass` | `string` |  | button classes |
| `@svgClass` | `string` |  |  |
| `@fill` | `string` |  |  |
| `@title` | `string` |  | Text for an SVG `<title>` element inside the icon, making it accessible to screen readers. Matches `@carbon/icons-react`'s `children` pattern (callers pass `<title>{description}</title>` as children). An empty string renders an empty `<title></title>`, matching React's behaviour when a description prop is present but empty. |

IconIndicator

preview-statusindicators-preview-iconindicator · ./src/components/icon-indicator.stories.gts
Icon indicators pair a status icon with a label to communicate the state of an item. They support the kinds `failed`, `caution-major`, `caution-minor`, `undefined`, `succeeded`, `normal`, `in-progress`, `incomplete`, `not-started`, `pending`, `unknown`, and `informative`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-start" \| "top-end" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "left-end" \| "left-start" \| "right-end" \| "right-start"` |  | Specify how the tooltip should align with the icon in compact mode |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Will auto-align the tooltip in compact mode so it stays within the viewport, flipping to the opposite side when it would otherwise overflow |
| `@compact` | `boolean` |  | When true, displays only the icon with the label in a tooltip |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Description for the icon announced to screen readers in compact mode. Defaults to `label` when not provided. |
| `@kind` (required) | `"undefined" \| "failed" \| "caution-major" \| "caution-minor" \| "succeeded" \| "normal" \| "in-progress" \| "incomplete" \| "not-started" \| "pending" \| "unknown" \| "informative"` |  | Specify the kind of icon to be used |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | Label next to the icon |
| `@size` | `16 \| 20` |  | Specify the size of the Icon Indicator. Defaults to 16. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

InlineLoading

components-inlineloading · ./src/components/inline-loading.stories.gts
Shows that something is in progress, finished or failed, in place of the control that started it. `@status` is `inactive`, `active` (the default), `finished` or `error`; `@description` is the text next to the icon, and `@iconDescription` labels the icon. `@onSuccess` runs `@successDelay` milliseconds (1500 by default) after the status becomes `finished`, which is the moment to swap the original control back in.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@status` | `InlineLoadingStatus` |  | The loading status. Defaults to `"active"`. |
| `@description` | `string` |  | Text shown next to the icon. |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Labels the icon. Defaults to "loading", or to the status when it's finished or an error. |
| `@onSuccess` | `() => void` |  | Called `@successDelay` milliseconds after `@status` becomes `"finished"`. |
| `@successDelay` | `number` |  | How long to wait before calling `@onSuccess`, in milliseconds. Defaults to 1500. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import InlineLoading from 'carbon-components-ember/components/inline-loading';
Ux Example story ok

      @onSuccess={{submission.reset}}
    />
  {{else}}
    <Button {{on "click" submission.submit.perform}}>Submit</Button>
  {{/if}}
</div>

Layer

components-layer · ./src/components/layer.stories.gts
The `Layer` component renders content on a specific Carbon layer. Each layer has a set of token values associated with it, which other components (like `Tile`) key off of to determine their own background. You can use these tokens directly, or use contextual tokens from Carbon's styles package like `$layer` or `$field`. `Layer`s can be nested up to three levels deep; past that, the level stays clamped at the third level. Ember has no equivalent of React's ambient `LayerContext`, so a bare `<Layer>` always renders as the first level of nesting; to nest `Layer`s more than one level deep, use the component yielded to the block, which is pre-bound to the correct next level: ```hbs <Layer as |L|> ... <L>...</L> </Layer> ```
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | Specify the element type to render, defaults to `div` |
| `@level` | `LayerLevel` |  | Specify the layer level and override any existing level based on hierarchy. Defaults to `1`, which matches the page's implicit base layer (see `<Theme>`, which applies `cds--layer-one` at the root). |
| `@withBackground` | `boolean` |  | Applies a background color set to the layer's `$layer-background` token |

## Blocks

- default block: Yields a `Layer` pre-bound to the correct next nesting level. Ember has no equivalent of React's ambient `LayerContext`, so a bare `<Layer>` always renders as if it were the first level of nesting (matching the common case); use the yielded component to nest `Layer`s more than one level deep so each one's level increments correctly.
  - yields `Layer` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

Layout

preview-preview-layout · ./src/components/layout.stories.gts
The `Layout` component provides a way to set layout contexts for specific parts of an application. It uses Carbon's experimental `layout` Sass module to control layout-related settings like size and density for all components rendered within it that support these options. All children components that support it will react to the `@size` and `@density` you pass to `Layout`. Note that not all components support the entire spectrum of options available; in these cases a component will typically cap out at the maximum or minimum size it supports. If a component is outside of a layout context, or `@size` / `@density` isn't set, it falls back to its default rendering.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render Layout as. |
| `@density` | `LayoutDensity` |  | Specify the desired density of components within this layout. |
| `@size` | `LayoutSize` |  | Specify the desired size of components within this layout. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import Layout from 'carbon-components-ember/components/layout';

    <br />
    <Demo />
  </div>
  <div>
    <h2>Inside of &lt;Layout&gt;</h2>
    <br />
    <Layout @size="md" @density="normal">
      <Demo />
    </Layout>
  </div>
</Stack>

</Layout>

</LayoutConstraint>

LayoutConstraint

preview-preview-layout-layoutconstraint · ./src/components/layout-constraint.stories.gts
Applies layout constraints to its children that might differ from their own preference or from the surrounding `Layout` context. The constraints for each group (`@size` and `@density`) are passed as an object with any of the keys `min`, `default` and `max`, e.g. `{{hash default="sm" min="sm" max="lg"}}`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render LayoutConstraint as. |
| `@density` | `LayoutConstraintValue` |  | Specify the desired layout density constraints of this element's children. |
| `@size` | `LayoutConstraintValue` |  | Specify the desired layout size constraints of this element's children. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

LayoutDirection

components-layoutdirection · ./src/components/layout-direction.stories.gts
The `LayoutDirection` component sets the reading direction (`ltr` or `rtl`) for a part of the page. It renders a wrapper element with a `dir` attribute, which the browser natively cascades to descendant elements. `LayoutDirection` components can be nested to override the direction for a specific section of content. The block receives `dir` and `isRTL` so nested content can react to the active direction, mirroring React's `useLayoutDirection` hook.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@dir` (required) | `LayoutDirectionType` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `dir`: `LayoutDirectionType`
    - `isRTL`: `boolean`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

  </p>
  <LayoutDirection @dir="rtl">

Links are used as navigational elements. They may be used on their own, within a sentence or paragraph, or directly following the content they are relevant to.
API description

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

Markdown

ai-chat-markdown · ./src/components/ai-chat/markdown.stories.gts
`Markdown` parses `@markdown` with `markdown-it` (CommonMark, plus tables, strikethrough, autolinking, GFM task lists, and `==highlight==` extended syntax) and renders it as sanitized, Carbon-styled HTML. Unlike upstream's `cds-aichat-markdown`, rendered HTML is **always** run through DOMPurify before being injected, regardless of `@sanitizeHTML` — see the component's class doc for the full reasoning. Set `@removeHTML={{true}}` to strip raw HTML from the source entirely instead of just sanitizing it.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@markdown` | `string` |  | Direct markdown source input. Always-controlled, always-authoritative. |
| `@sanitizeHTML` | `boolean` |  | Accepted for API parity with upstream's `sanitize-html` attribute, but not wired to anything: this port always sanitizes rendered HTML via DOMPurify, regardless of this flag. See `-markdown-render.ts`'s `renderMarkdown` doc for why. |
| `@removeHTML` | `boolean` |  | Strip all raw HTML from the parsed markdown. Defaults to `false`. |
| `@streaming` | `boolean` |  | Throttles re-render to at most once per 100ms (leading + trailing), matching upstream's own default streaming throttle - reduces layout thrash while a caller is appending markdown token-by-token. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
