Menu

components-menu · ./src/components/menu.stories.gts
Menu is a low-level building block for rendering a floating list of actions; `OverflowMenu` and context menus are built on top of it. It's a controlled component: pass `@open` and toggle it from `@onClose`/your own trigger. Compose it out of `MenuItem`, `MenuItemDivider`, `MenuItemGroup`, `MenuItemRadioGroup`, and `MenuItemSelectable`. By default the Menu renders into `document.body`; `@target` renders it into another element. `@x`/`@y` position it; passing both edges of a trigger (`[x1, x2]`/`[y1, y2]`) lets it flip to the other side when it doesn't fit. Clicking a leaf item, pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd>, or moving focus outside the menu all call `@onClose`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | A required label describing the Menu (used as `aria-label`). |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the Menu is open or not. |
| `@backgroundToken` | `"layer" \| "background"` |  | Specify the background token to use. Default is 'layer'. |
| `@border` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a border should be rendered on the menu. |
| `@menuAlignment` | `string` |  | Specify how the menu should align with the button element. Only `top`/`top-start`/`top-end` affect rendering (adds a top box-shadow). |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  | Specify the size of the Menu. Only respected on the top-level Menu; submenus always inherit the size of their root Menu. |
| `@target` | `Element` |  | Specify a DOM node where the Menu should be rendered in. Defaults to `document.body`. Pass a node inside your own root when the Menu is rendered in a shadow root, otherwise it escapes into the light DOM where your styles don't reach it. Submenus aren't portaled - they inherit this as their positioning origin instead. |
| `@x` | `number \| [number, number]` |  | Specify the x position of the Menu. Either pass a single number or an array with two numbers describing your activator's boundaries ([x1, x2]). |
| `@y` | `number \| [number, number]` |  | Specify the y position of the Menu. Either pass a single number or an array with two numbers describing your activator's boundaries ([y1, y2]). |
| `@onOpen` | `() => void` |  | Provide an optional function to be called when the Menu is opened. |
| `@onClose` | `() => void` |  | Provide an optional function to be called when the Menu should be closed, including if the Menu is blurred, the user presses escape, or the Menu is a submenu and the user presses ArrowLeft. |
| `@isRoot` | `boolean` |  |  |

NumberInput allows the user to enter a number, and to increment/decrement the value using stepper buttons. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled input, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it; `@onChange` receives the new value, the event and the stepper direction.

OrderedList

components-orderedlist · ./src/components/ordered-list.stories.gts
Ordered lists are groupings of related content where the order of the items within the group is meaningful. Each item is a `ListItem`: a single `<li>` with the styles it needs to work as a child of `OrderedList` or `UnorderedList`. It has no arguments of its own; any attributes passed to it (`id`, `class`, ...) are applied to the underlying `<li>`. A `ListItem` can contain a nested list to build multi-level lists.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@nested` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@native` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isExpressive` | `boolean` |  |  |

components-overflowmenu · ./src/components/overflow-menu.stories.gts

No description found. Write a jsdoc comment such as /** Component description */.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@icon` | `typeof Icon` |  |  |
| `@direction` (required) | `"top" \| "bottom"` |  | The side of the trigger the menu opens on, when there's room for it there; otherwise it opens on the other side. |
| `@flipped` | `boolean` |  | Aligns the menu's end edge with the trigger's, as Carbon React's `flipped`. |
| `@tooltip` | `string` |  |  |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Names the trigger for assistive technology, as Carbon React's `iconDescription`. Defaults to `@tooltip`, or "Options". |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@danger` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@eventType` | `"click" \| "mousedown"` |  |  |
| `@horizontalPosition` | `"right" \| "left" \| "center" \| "auto" \| "auto-right"` |  | Passed straight through to the underlying `BasicDropdown` (whose own declared type isn't cleanly importable - its published `.d.ts` re-exports it from a sibling module via a broken `.ts`-extension specifier). Defaults to `'auto'` (`'right'` with `@flipped`) - only needed when the trigger sits near the right edge of a container narrower than the viewport, where `'auto'` would otherwise pick `'left'` (fits the viewport) and let the menu overflow that container instead. |

PasswordInput

components-passwordinput · ./src/components/password-input.stories.gts
PasswordInput allows the user to enter a single line of text that is masked by default, with a toggle button to reveal or hide the value. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled field, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it. `@type="text"` starts with the value shown.

Popover

components-popover · ./src/components/popover.stories.gts
`Popover` is used for triggering a pop-up next to a trigger element, typically a button, in a given direction. It is a controlled component: the consumer owns the `@open` argument and toggles it (usually from the trigger's click handler), while `Popover` calls `@onRequestClose` whenever the user clicks outside of the popover or presses <kbd>Escape</kbd> while focus is inside the popover content. The trigger element and `PopoverContent` are both yielded as plain children of `Popover`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `PopoverAlignment` |  | Specify how the popover should align with the trigger element. |
| `@alignmentAxisOffset` | `number` |  | **Experimental:** Provide an offset value for alignment axis. Only takes effect when `autoAlign` is enabled. Not currently implemented in this Ember port. |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render the outermost node as. |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Will auto-align the popover on first render if it is not visible within the viewport (or `autoAlignBoundary`, if provided). |
| `@autoAlignBoundary` | `HTMLElement` |  | Specify a bounding element to be used for autoAlign calculations. The viewport is used by default. |
| `@backgroundToken` | `"layer" \| "background"` |  | Specify the background token to use. Default is 'layer'. |
| `@border` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a border should be rendered on the popover. |
| `@caret` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a caret should be rendered. |
| `@dropShadow` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a drop shadow should be rendered on the popover. |
| `@highContrast` | `boolean` |  | Render the component using the high-contrast variant. |
| `@isTabTip` | `boolean` |  | Render the component using the tab tip variant. |
| `@onRequestClose` | `() => void` |  | Specify a handler for closing the popover. The handler should take care of closing the popover, e.g. changing the `open` argument. Called when the user clicks outside of the popover or presses Escape while focus is inside the popover content. |
| `@open` (required) | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the component is currently open or closed. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import Popover from 'carbon-components-ember/components/popover';

Tab Tip story ok 
<div style="display: flex">
  <Popover
    @open={{one.state.open}}
    @align="bottom-start"
    @isTabTip={{true}}
    @onRequestClose={{one.close}}
  >
    <button
      type="button"
      aria-label="Settings"
      aria-expanded={{if one.state.open "true" "false"}}
      {{on "click" one.toggle}}
    >
      <Settings />
    </button>
    <PopoverContent style="padding: 1rem;">
      <RadioButtonGroup
        @name="radio-button-group"
        @defaultSelected="small"
        @orientation="vertical"
      >
        <:heading>Row height 1</:heading>
        <:default as |Radio|>

        </:default>
      </RadioButtonGroup>

        <legend class="cds--label">Edit columns</legend>
        <Checkbox @label="Name" @checked={{true}} />
        <Checkbox @label="Type" @checked={{true}} />
        <Checkbox @label="Location" @checked={{true}} />
      </fieldset>
    </PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  <Popover

PromptLine

ai-chat-prompt-line · ./src/components/ai-chat/prompt-line.stories.gts
`PromptLine` is the editing surface of the chat input stack, typically composed inside a `PromptLineShell`'s `<:editor>` block. It renders a plain `<textarea>` by default and never statically imports `@tiptap/*` — setting `@rich` (or calling `ensureEditor()` off the handle `@onReady` provides) dynamically loads a small Tiptap runtime chunk and upgrades the surface in place, carrying the text, caret, and focus over losslessly. Both modes share the same `@content`/`@onChange`/`@onSendIntent` contract. `@content` is always-controlled: typing only fires `@onChange`, so the host keeps the text and hands it back. Press Enter to send (Shift+Enter inserts a newline instead). `@extensions` accepts plain Tiptap `Extension`s appended to the base Carbon bundle (schema, undo/redo, placeholder, plain-text paste, the Enter/Mod-Enter/Escape keymap) — memoize the array you pass, since a fresh one every render rebuilds the live editor (content, selection, and focus survive; undo history doesn't). ### Mention, command, autocomplete, and starter triggers `buildCarbonExtensions` (and the individual `carbonMention`/`carbonCommand`/`carbonAutocomplete`/`carbonStarterTrigger` factories it wraps, all under `carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/-prompt-line/tiptap/`) build Tiptap extensions you pass through `@extensions` like any other — `PromptLine` itself has no dedicated mention/command/autocomplete/starter args, matching upstream's own `<cds-aichat-prompt-line>`. The extensions only dispatch a bubbling `cds-aichat-trigger-change` DOM event with `{ type, query, triggerOffset }`; **the actual popup is `PromptLineAutocomplete`** — pair it with a `PromptLine` via the imperative handle from `@onReady`. A command chip (`/summarize`) is prefixed with its trigger character by default; a mention chip (`Jane Smith`) isn't — either default can be overridden per-config or per-item via `showTriggerInChip`. Mention, command, autocomplete, and starter extensions each react to the *same* document changes and dispatch `cds-aichat-trigger-change` independently — combined on one editor, typing `@` after focusing an empty field can dispatch the starter list's own exit event (`null`) *after* the mention trigger's own opening event. A naive "last event wins" listener can momentarily see a stale `null` and hide its popup even though a trigger is genuinely open. `PromptLineAutocomplete` reconciles this (batches same-tick events by microtask, resolves to the last non-null one) — see the **All triggers** story.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@content` | `string` |  | Current plain-text value. Always-controlled: typing only fires `@onChange`. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Message'`. |
| `@testId` | `string` |  |  |
| `@autofocus` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Fires with the new value on every input, in either mode. |
| `@onSendIntent` | `() => void` |  | Fires on plain Enter (non-empty field) or Mod-Enter (any field), mirroring upstream's Enter-to-send keymap. Identical in both modes. |
| `@rich` | `boolean` |  | Selects the rich Tiptap editor. Defaults to the textarea. The element lazy-loads Tiptap (a dynamic `import()`, so a chat that never sets this never ships it) and upgrades the textarea to it in place — text, caret, and focus all carry over, so the swap is a same-frame handoff, not a visible reset. The upgrade is **sticky**: once rich, later setting this back to `false` does not downgrade. |
| `@extensions` | `Extension<any, any>[]` |  | Host-supplied Tiptap `Extension`s, appended to the base Carbon bundle (schema, undo/redo, placeholder, plain-text paste, the Enter/Mod-Enter/ Escape keymap) when the rich editor (re)builds. Ignored in textarea mode — setting these alone does not trigger the upgrade. Compared by reference: a fresh array every render rebuilds the live editor (preserving content/selection/focus but resetting undo history), so memoize it rather than passing an inline literal. |
| `@onReady` | `(api: PromptLineApi) => void` |  | Called once, right after mount, with an imperative handle to the surface. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

PromptLineAutocomplete

ai-chat-prompt-line-autocomplete · ./src/components/ai-chat/prompt-line-autocomplete.stories.gts
The suggestion overlay for `PromptLine`'s mention (`@`), command (`/`), autocomplete, and starter-prompt Tiptap extensions (see **AI Chat/Prompt line** for building those). Pair one `PromptLineAutocomplete` with exactly one `PromptLine` via the imperative handle from its `@onReady` — typically composed inside a `PromptLineShell`'s `<:autocompleteContent>` block. Mention and command items always insert into the editor as a chip (a `data-token-type="mention"`/`"command"` node — `disableDirectSend` is forced `true` for these two regardless of config). Autocomplete and starter items default to **sending directly**: clicking one fires `@onItemSend` with its `value ?? label` and never touches the editor at all — the host owns actually sending it (this component carries no chat-domain logic, matching `PromptLineShell`). Set `disableDirectSend: true` on an autocomplete/starters config to switch that trigger's items to the "insert into the editor" path instead, firing `@onItemSelected` (and, for starters specifically, `@onStarterSelected` with the editor's full text) rather than `@onItemSend`. Use the arrow keys, Home/End, Enter and Escape from the editor; disabled items are skipped.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@promptLine` | `PromptLineApi` |  | The `PromptLineApi` handle from the paired `PromptLine`'s `@onReady`. Read only inside event handlers (click, keydown, outside-click) — never during render/modifier setup — so there is no ordering requirement against when the paired `PromptLine`'s `@onReady` actually fires. |
| `@mention` | `TriggerSuggestionConfig` |  | `@`-style mention trigger config. |
| `@command` | `TriggerSuggestionConfig` |  | `/`-style command trigger config. |
| `@autocomplete` | `BaseSuggestionConfig` |  | Live-typeahead autocomplete config (no trigger character). |
| `@starters` | `StartersConfig` |  | Starter prompts shown while the editor is empty and focused. |
| `@isSendDisabled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, the "send directly" click path (see `BaseSuggestionConfig.disableDirectSend`) becomes a no-op instead of firing `@onItemSend`. |
| `@i18n` | `Partial<AutocompleteI18n>` |  |  |
| `@headerConfig` | `HeaderConfig` |  |  |
| `@onStarterSelected` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Fires after a starter is inserted into the editor (the `disableDirectSend: true` path only) with the editor's full raw text, so the host can trigger send. Skipped when `@isSendDisabled`. |
| `@onItemSelected` | `(item: SuggestionItem) => void` |  | Fires after any item is inserted into the editor (the `disableDirectSend: true` path, all trigger types). |
| `@onItemSend` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Fires when an item is activated on the default "send directly" path (`disableDirectSend` unset/false) with the item's `value ?? label` — this component never touches the editor for this path, the host owns actually sending. Skipped (and the popup stays open) when `@isSendDisabled`. |
| `@target` | `HTMLElement` |  | Ancestor element to listen on for the bubbling `cds-aichat-trigger-change` DOM event, editor keydown forwarding, and outside-click/focusout detection. Defaults to the closest `.cds-aichat-prompt-line-shell` ancestor, or this component's own parent element if there isn't one — override for standalone use (a `PromptLine` not inside a `PromptLineShell`), same spirit as `Menu`'s `@target`/`DatePicker`'s `@appendTo`. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

PromptLineShell

ai-chat-prompt-line-shell · ./src/components/ai-chat/prompt-line-shell.stories.gts
Layout-only composer chrome for the chat input: `PromptLineShell` defines six named blocks (`<:editor>`, `<:messageActions>`, `<:fileUploads>`, `<:autocompleteContent>`, `<:fieldMessaging>`, `<:sendControl>`) and the spacing/border treatment around them. It carries no chat-domain logic and forwards no editor methods — compose a `PromptLine` (or your own editing surface) into `<:editor>`. See **AI Chat/Prompt line** for compositions with message actions, file uploads and the autocomplete popup.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@rounded` | `boolean` |  | Reflects to a class so consumer CSS can target the rounded variant. |
| `@expanded` | `boolean` |  | Expanded layout: the editor fills its own full-width row, with the message actions and send control on a second row beneath it. The reflow is driven purely by a container class — the rendered DOM is identical in both modes. |
| `@hasError` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hasFileUploads` | `boolean` |  | Whether the `<:fileUploads>` block currently has real uploads to show. Upstream derives this by watching the slotted file-uploads element's own `has-uploads` attribute via a `MutationObserver`; Ember has no equivalent DOM-introspection hook for a block's rendered content, so this port takes it as a plain controlled arg instead — pass it straight through from whatever tracks the upload list. |

## Blocks

- `<:editor>`: A `PromptLine` (or equivalent) the caller owns directly; no fallback is rendered.
- `<:messageActions>`: Action icons beside the text area.
- `<:fileUploads>`: Visual list of files being uploaded.
- `<:autocompleteContent>`: Suggestion overlay above the input.
- `<:fieldMessaging>`: Inline error / status content beneath the autocomplete row.
- `<:sendControl>`: Send / stop-streaming button.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

RadioButton

components-radiobutton · ./src/components/radio-button.stories.gts
Radio buttons are used when there is a list of two or more options that are mutually exclusive and the user must select exactly one choice. Render them through a `RadioButtonGroup`, which yields a `RadioButton` already wired to the group: the group owns the shared `name`, the selection (`@defaultSelected`, or `@valueSelected` to control it) and reports changes through `@onChange`. A RadioButton can also be used on its own with `@checked`/`@defaultChecked`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@value` | `Value` |  |  |
| `@name` | `string` |  |  |
| `@checked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@labelPosition` | `"right" \| "left"` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@group` | `RadioButtonGroup` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: Value \| undefined, name: string \| undefined, event: Event) => void` |  |  |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block: The label's content. Keep it text: put an AI label or other controls in `<:decorator>`.
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown after the label. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it; with `@kind="inline"`, also pass `@size="md"`.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

RadioButtonGroup

components-radiobutton-radiobuttongroup · ./src/components/radio-button/group.stories.gts
A `<fieldset>` that groups mutually exclusive `RadioButton`s. It yields a `RadioButton` already wired to the group: the group owns the shared `name`, the selection (`@defaultSelected`, or `@valueSelected` to control it) and reports changes through `@onChange`. The legend is `@legendText`, or the `heading` block for richer content. See `RadioButton` for the buttons themselves.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` |  |  |
| `@labelPosition` | `"right" \| "left"` |  |  |
| `@legendText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@name` | `string` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@valueSelected` | `Value` |  |  |
| `@defaultSelected` | `Value` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: Value \| undefined, name: string \| undefined, event: Event) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:heading>`: The legend's content. Keep it text: put an AI label in `<:decorator>`.
- default block
  - yields `RadioButton` (component)
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown after the legend. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it; keep its default kind, as Carbon React does.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLFieldSetElement`.

  <Radio @labelText="Radio button label" @value="radio-2" />

ReasoningSteps

ai-chat-reasoning-steps · ./src/components/ai-chat/reasoning-steps.stories.gts
Displays a list of reasoning steps. Supports auto-open/close behavior or fully controlled state managed by the host. `ReasoningSteps` and its yielded `ReasoningStep` render a collapsible list of model-reasoning steps for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat) — the same disclosure shape as `ChainOfThought`, but without step numbering or status icons. A step without body content renders a static (non-interactive) header. Passing `@controlled={{true}}` to `ReasoningSteps` propagates `@controlled` to every yielded step: each step's own `@open` becomes the sole source of truth, and a click only calls `@onToggle`. The `Step*` stories mirror upstream's separate `Reasoning steps/Step` stories: `ReasoningStep` is only available as the component `ReasoningSteps` yields.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel that wraps this reasoning-steps list is open. |
| `@controlled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, propagated to every yielded step as its own `@controlled`. |

## Blocks

- default block: Renders one `<ReasoningStep>` per step. Yields the step component pre-bound with `@controlled`, mirroring `Layer`'s `WithBoundArgs` pattern.
  - yields `ReasoningStep` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

      <Markdown @markdown={{step.body}} />

</ReasoningSteps>

ReasoningStepsToggle

ai-chat-reasoning-steps-toggle · ./src/components/ai-chat/reasoning-steps-toggle.stories.gts
A dedicated toggle button for expanding or collapsing reasoning steps. Compose it with `ReasoningSteps` when you want to manage the open state externally. The toggle is DOM-decoupled from the panel (same as `ChainOfThoughtToggle`/`ChainOfThought`): point `@panelId` at the `ReasoningSteps`' own `id` for `aria-controls`. With `@onToggle`, `@open` is controlled; without it, `@open` only seeds the initial state.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel this toggle controls is open. |
| `@openLabelText` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Hide reasoning steps'`. |
| `@closedLabelText` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Show reasoning steps'`. |
| `@panelId` | `string` |  | `aria-controls` target — typically a `ReasoningSteps`' own id. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onToggle` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new open state whenever the button is clicked. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLButtonElement`.

Resizer

utilities-resizer · ./src/components/resizer.stories.gts
A draggable (and keyboard-operable) handle placed between two sibling elements. By default `Resizer` resizes its previous and next DOM siblings directly as it's dragged; pass `@onResize` to take full control instead (for example, to drive a CSS Grid's `grid-template-columns`). Any content passed to the default block is rendered inside the handle, which is useful for a custom drag icon. Drag the handle with a mouse, or focus it and use the arrow keys (hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> for larger steps, or press <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> to jump to a boundary). Double-clicking the handle resets the siblings to the size they had when it was inserted. By design, the resting handle is a subtle `border-subtle`-colored 4px bar, much more visible on hover/focus (`border-interactive`). Carbon's docs suggest enhancing the trigger cue with a pseudo-element or custom children if needed; every story here widens the hit area with an invisible `::before`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@orientation` (required) | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` |  | Whether the resizer handle is oriented horizontally (resize up/down) or vertically (resize left/right). |
| `@onResize` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, delta: number) => void` |  | Called on every resize movement with the delta (px) from the drag/key start position. When provided the component becomes fully controlled — sibling sizes are NOT updated automatically. |
| `@onResizeEnd` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, element: HTMLDivElement) => void` |  | Called once when a resize interaction ends (mouse-up, or a debounced moment after the last key-driven resize). Receives the resizer's element. |
| `@onDoubleClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Called on double-click. When provided, the default reset-to-initial- sizes behavior is suppressed. |
| `@thickness` | `number` |  | Thickness of the handle in px. Defaults to 4. |

## Blocks

- default block: Optional content rendered inside the handle (e.g. custom drag icons).

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

Search

components-search · ./src/components/search.stories.gts
Search allows users to enter a term to be used to find specific content, filtering out results that don't match. `@onChange` is called with the term 200ms after the user stops typing (a pending call is cancelled by the next keystroke), and again with an empty value when the field is cleared with its close button, which also calls `@onClear`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string \| null) => void \| TaskInstance<unknown> \| undefined` |  |  |
| `@onClear` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@value` | `string` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  |  |
| `@isLoading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@expandable` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@closeButtonLabelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@autoComplete` | `string` |  |  |
| `@type` | `string` |  |  |

Select

components-select · ./src/components/select.stories.gts
A select lets the user pick one option (or several, with `@multiple`) from a dropdown list. Select is controlled: pass `@selected` and update it from `@onSelect`. Options can be any value; the block renders each one. The dropdown renders through ember-basic-dropdown's wormhole (`#ember-basic-dropdown-wormhole`) unless `@renderInPlace` is set.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@options` (required) | `T[]` |  |  |
| `@searchField` | `string` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@loadingMessage` | `string` |  |  |
| `@searchPlaceholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabelledBy` | `string` |  | id of an element that labels the select, for a visible label rendered outside it (e.g. Pagination's "Items per page:"). Otherwise `@title` is the label, and the placeholder names it as a last resort. |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@title` | `string` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@inline` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@showNumber` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@searchEnabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@renderInPlace` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@addItem` | `(item: T) => void` |  |  |
| `@removeItem` | `(item: T) => void` |  |  |
| `@selected` | `T[] \| NonNullable<T>` |  |  |
| `@multiple` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onSelect` | `((item: T[]) => void) \| ((item: T) => void)` |  |  |
| `@onOpen` | `((select: Select<T, true>, e: Event \| undefined) => boolean \| void \| undefined) \| ((select: Select<T, false>, e: Event \| undefined) => boolean \| void \| undefined)` |  |  |
| `@search` | `((term: string, select: Select<T, true>) => void \| Promise<void> \| readonly T[] \| Promise<readonly T[]>) \| ((term: string, select: Select<T, false>) => void \| Promise<void> \| readonly T[] \| Promise<readonly T[]>)` |  |  |
| `@selectFocused` | `((select: Select<T, true>, event: FocusEvent) => void) \| ((select: Select<T, false>, event: FocusEvent) => void)` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `option` (`Option<T>`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `Element`.

SelectItem

components-selectitem · ./src/components/select-item.stories.gts
`SelectItem` renders a native `<option>` element for use inside a native `<select>`. Group options with `SelectItemGroup`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@value` (required) | `string` |  | Specify the value of the <SelectItem> |
| `@text` (required) | `string` |  | Provide the contents of your <SelectItem> |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the <SelectItem> should be disabled |
| `@hidden` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the <SelectItem> is hidden |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLOptionElement`.

ai-chat-session-shell · ./src/components/ai-chat/session-shell.stories.gts
Info
No description found. Write a jsdoc comment such as /** Component description */.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@aiEnabled` | `boolean` |  | Enables AI-specific theming on the launcher and shell. |
| `@closedLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the closed launcher button. |
| `@messagesAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the messages region. |
| `@instanceId` | `string` |  | Resolves which `ChatSession` this shell drives, via `@service('carbon.ai-chat-session').for(instanceId)` - for isolating several independent chat widgets on one page. Omit it for a single-widget page (resolves to the default session, matching this component's pre-multi-instance behavior). |
| `@historyItems` | `SessionShellHistoryItem[]` |  | Host-supplied list of past chat history items, rendered by `SessionShell`'s own default `<:history>` assembly (a `ChatHistory` built from `ChatHistoryHeader`/`Toolbar`/`Content`/`Panel`) - pass a `<:history>` block instead for full control. Host-owned rather than tracked by `carbon.ai-chat-session` itself, matching upstream's own division of responsibility (`HistoryService#loadHistory()`'s `customLoadHistory` host callback, not a Redux store slice) - see AGENTS.md. |
| `@selectedHistoryItemId` | `string` |  | Id of the currently-selected history item. |
| `@onHistoryItemSelect` | `(id: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@onHistoryItemRename` | `(id: string, name: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@onHistoryItemDelete` | `(id: string) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:header>`: Shell header content, shown only while open.
- `<:history>`: History panel content. Overrides `SessionShell`'s own default `ChatHistory` assembly entirely when passed - see `@historyItems` and AGENTS.md's "Persistence and the `chat-history` integration" section for the session-owned/host-owned split the default assembly draws. This component only owns `@service('carbon.ai-chat-session').for(@instanceId).showHistory`/ `toggleHistory`, the same "inject the service, pass args down, don't prop-drill" boundary `ChatShell` itself already draws for every other slot - a filler that needs the same session this shell drives must resolve it with the same `@instanceId` this shell was given.
- `<:workspace>`: Workspace panel content. Left entirely to the caller - see `<:history>`.

Slider

components-slider · ./src/components/slider.stories.gts
Sliders provide a visual indication of adjustable content, where the user can increase or decrease the value by moving the handle along a horizontal track. Slider is controlled: pass `@value` (and `@valueUpper` for a second handle) and update them from `@onChange`, which receives `{ value, valueUpper }`. The handles move with the pointer or the arrow keys (Shift multiplies the step by `@stepMultiplier`), and the text input(s) next to the track accept typed values.

Stack

layout-stack · ./src/components/stack.stories.gts
The Stack component is a useful layout utility in a component-based model. This allows components to not use margin and instead delegate the responsibility of positioning and layout to parent components. Stack uses the spacing scale from the Design Language in order to determine how much space there should be between items rendered by the Stack component. It also supports a custom `@gap` argument which will allow a user to provide a custom value for the gap of the layout (a number from 1 to 13 picks a step of the spacing scale; a string sets any CSS gap value). This component supports both horizontal and vertical orientations.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render the stack as. |
| `@gap` | `string \| number` |  | The spacing between items in the stack. Provide a number between 1 and 13 to use one of the steps in the spacing scale, or a string to set a custom CSS gap value. |
| `@orientation` | `StackOrientation` |  | The direction items are stacked in. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

Accepted for parity with upstream, but not wired: the shared `Pagination` component this addon already has hardcodes that label rather than accepting an override, and changing `Pagination` itself is out of scope here. |

| `@defaultPageSize` | `number` |  | Initial page size. Upstream calculates this from the rendered component's width (10 above ~400px, 5 below); this port skips that DOM-measurement heuristic and simply defaults to `5`. |

Tabs

components-tabs · ./src/components/tabs.stories.gts
`Tabs` yields a bound `TabPane` component for each tab; its block is the tab's panel. The active tab can be uncontrolled (the first enabled tab, or the one with `@isDefault`) or controlled with `@selectedTab` / `@tabSelected`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@selectedTab` | `string` |  |  |
| `@tabSelected` | `(tab: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@loading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@contained` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Size of the tabs. `sm` and `md` apply to line tabs; `lg` only takes effect when `@contained` is also set (a no-op on line tabs otherwise). |
| `@fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | When `@contained`, stretches tabs to fill the available width in equal shares. |
| `@activation` | `"manual" \| "automatic"` |  | `automatic` (default) selects a tab as soon as it receives keyboard focus. `manual` only moves focus with the arrow keys; Enter/Space selects the focused tab. |
| `@dismissable` | `boolean` |  | Renders a close button on every tab. Requires `@onTabCloseRequest`. |
| `@onTabCloseRequest` | `(tab: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `TabPane` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import Tabs from 'carbon-components-ember/components/tabs';
Default story ok 
<Tabs
  @contained={{false}}
  @size={{@size}}
  @fullWidth={{@fullWidth}}
  @activation="automatic"
  @ariaLabel={{@ariaLabel}}
  @tabSelected={{@tabSelected}}
  as |TabPane|
>
  {{#each args.tabs as |tab index|}}
    <TabPane
      @title={{tab.title}}
      @disabled={{tab.disabled}}
      @renderIcon={{tab.icon}}
      @secondaryLabel={{tab.secondaryLabel}}
      @isDefault={{isFirst index}}
    >
      Tab Panel
      {{index}}
    </TabPane>
  {{/each}}
</Tabs>

preview-preview-text · ./src/components/text.stories.gts
`Text` renders content wrapped in an element with the appropriate `dir` attribute set (`auto` by default), so that bidirectional text (mixing left-to-right and right-to-left scripts) is displayed and aligned correctly. Use `@as` to change the element (defaults to `span`). `TextDirection` sets a text direction for all of the content rendered inside of it, which is useful for wrapping a subtree that should use a fixed or auto-detected direction.
API description

TextArea allows the user to enter multiple lines of text. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled field, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it; `@onChange` receives the new value and the event.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@value` | `string` |  |  |
| `@defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@rows` | `number` |  |  |
| `@cols` | `number` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@enableCounter` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@maxCount` | `number` |  |  |
| `@counterMode` | `"character" \| "word"` |  |  |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string, event: Event) => void` |  |  |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  |  |
| `@onKeyDown` | `(event: KeyboardEvent) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import TextArea from 'carbon-components-ember/components/text-area';
Default story ok 
<TextArea @labelText="Text Area label" @helperText="TextArea helper text" @placeholder="Placeholder text" @rows={{4}} @maxCount={{500}} @enableCounter={{true}}>
  <:decorator as |AILabel|>{{yield AILabel}}</:decorator>
</TextArea>
With Layer story ok

</TextArea>
With AI Label story ok

    <AILabel @align="bottom-end" as |label|>
      <label.Content><AIExplanation /></label.Content>
    </AILabel>
  </:decorator>
</TextArea>

  @value={{state.value}}
  @onChange={{onChange}}
/>
<p>value: {{state.value}}</p>

TextDirection

preview-preview-text-textdirection · ./src/components/text-direction.stories.gts
Sets a text direction (`@dir`: `ltr`, `rtl`, or `auto`, the default) for all of the content rendered inside of it, by wrapping it in an element (`@as`, a `div` by default) with that `dir`. Useful for a subtree of `Text` that should use a fixed or auto-detected direction.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@dir` | `TextDir` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import TextDirection from 'carbon-components-ember/components/text-direction';
Default story ok 
<TextDirection @as={{@as}} @dir="rtl">
  <Text @as="p">
    المغلوطة حول استنكار النشوة وتمجيد الألم نشأت بالفعل، وسأعرض لك التفاصيل
    لتكتشف حقيقة وأساس تلك السعادة البشرية.
  </Text>
  <Text @as="p">Hello world</Text>
</TextDirection>

Theme

components-theme · ./src/components/theme.stories.gts
The Theme component applies one of the Carbon themes (`white`, `g10`, `g90`, `g100`) to a section of your page. It renders a wrapper element with the corresponding Carbon zone class, which re-emits the theme's CSS custom properties scoped to that element — everything inside picks up the selected theme's tokens. The block receives `theme` and `isDark` so nested content can react to the active theme, mirroring React's `useTheme` hook. (The page-wide theme of these stories comes from the toolbar's theme switcher.)
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | Specify the element type to render, defaults to `div` |
| `@theme` | `CarbonTheme` |  | Specify the theme to apply to the contained content |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `theme`: `CarbonTheme`
    - `isDark`: `boolean`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import Theme from 'carbon-components-ember/components/theme';
Default story ok 
{{#each THEMES as |theme|}}
  <Theme @theme={{theme}}>
    <section style={{sectionStyle}}>{{theme}}</section>
  </Theme>
{{/each}}
useTheme story ok 
<div>
  <Theme @theme="g10" as |ctx|>
    <section style={{sectionStyle}}>
      <p>
        useTheme reveals... { theme: '{{ctx.theme}}', isDark: '{{ctx.isDark}}'}
      </p>
    </section>
  </Theme>
  <Theme @theme="g100" as |ctx|>
    <section style={{sectionStyle}}>
      <p>
        useTheme reveals... { theme: '{{ctx.theme}}', isDark: '{{ctx.isDark}}'}
      </p>
    </section>
  </Theme>
</div>
With Layer story ok 
<Stack @gap={{7}}>
  {{#each THEMES as |theme|}}
    <Theme @theme={{theme}}>
      <article style={{sectionStyle}}>
        <header style={{headerStyle}}>{{theme}} theme</header>
        <WithLayerTemplate>
          <div style={{layerContentStyle}}>Content</div>
        </WithLayerTemplate>
      </article>
    </Theme>
  {{/each}}
</Stack>

Tile

components-tile · ./src/components/tile.stories.gts
A tile is a highly flexible component for displaying a wide variety of content. `Tile` renders a default, `@clickable`, `@selectable` or `@expandable` tile; its `content`, `above` and `below` named blocks hold the content (`above`/`below` are the always-visible and expandable parts of an expandable tile). Use `TileGroup` together with its yielded `RadioTile` to build a group of tiles where only one tile can be selected at a time.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@selectable` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@clickable` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@expandable` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onClick` | `() => null` |  |  |
| `@onSelect` | `() => null` |  |  |
| `@tabindex` | `string` |  | Only applies to `@selectable` tiles - matches |
| `@id` | `string` |  | The id of the `@selectable` tile's root element, also used as the `for` target of its content `<label>`. Matches |

## Blocks

- `<:above>`
- `<:content>`
- `<:below>`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement | HTMLAnchorElement`.
Imports 
import Tile from 'carbon-components-ember/components/tile';
Default story ok

  <:content>
    Default tile

    <Link @href="https://www.carbondesignsystem.com">Link</Link>
  </:content>
</Tile>

</Tile>

TimePicker

components-timepicker · ./src/components/time-picker.stories.gts
`TimePicker` renders a text `<input>` for entering a time, optionally paired with one or more `TimePickerSelect` components (e.g. for AM/PM and time zone) rendered next to it, passed as the block. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled field, or `@value` with `@onChange` to make the `<input>` fully controlled.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Specify a custom `id` for the `<input>` |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  | Provide the text that will be read by a screen reader when visiting this control |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether you want the underlying label to be visually hidden |
| `@value` | `string` |  | Specify the value of the `<input>` |
| `@defaultValue` | `string` |  | Optionally provide the initial value of the `<input>` when uncontrolled |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  | Specify the placeholder attribute for the `<input>` |
| `@pattern` | `string` |  | Specify the regular expression working as the pattern of the time string in `<input>` |
| `@maxLength` | `number` |  | Specify the maximum length of the time string in `<input>` |
| `@type` | `string` |  | Specify the type of the `<input>` |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the Time Picker |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the `<input>` should be disabled |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the TimePicker should be read-only |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently invalid |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Provide the text that is displayed when the control is in an invalid state |
| `@warning` | `boolean` |  | Specify a warning message |
| `@warningText` | `string` |  | Provide the text that is displayed when the control is in a warning state |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  | The `light` prop for `TimePicker` has been deprecated. It will be removed in v12. Use the `Layer` component instead. |
| `@inputClassName` | `string` |  | Specify an optional className to be applied to the `<input>` node |
| `@pickerClassName` | `string` |  | Specify an optional className to be applied to the container that wraps the `<input>` and select option(s) |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string, event: Event) => void` |  | Optionally provide an `onChange` handler that is called whenever `<input>` is updated |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Optionally provide an `onClick` handler that is called whenever the `<input>` is clicked |
| `@onBlur` | `(event: FocusEvent) => void` |  | Optionally provide an `onBlur` handler that is called whenever the `<input>` loses focus |

## Blocks

- default block: Pass in `TimePickerSelect` components to render next to the `<input>`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import TimePicker from 'carbon-components-ember/components/time-picker';
Default story ok

  @labelText="Select a time"
  @hideLabel={{false}}
  @value={{@value}}
  @defaultValue={{@defaultValue}}
  @placeholder={{@placeholder}}
  @size={{@size}}
  @disabled={{false}}
  @readOnly={{@readOnly}}
  @invalid={{false}}
  @invalidText={{@invalidText}}
  @warning={{false}}

    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect @disabled={{false}}>

    <option value="Time zone 2">Time zone 2</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>

TimePickerSelect

components-timepicker-timepickerselect · ./src/components/time-picker/time-picker-select.stories.gts
A compact native `<select>` rendered next to the `TimePicker` field, e.g. for AM/PM or a time zone. Pass it, filled with `<option>`s, as the `TimePicker` block. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled select, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Specify a custom `id` for the `<select>` |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is disabled |
| `@value` | `string` |  | Specify the value of the `<select>` |
| `@defaultValue` | `string` |  | Optionally provide the default value of the `<select>` |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Specify an aria-label for the `<select>` (defaults to "open list of options") |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string, event: Event) => void` |  | Optionally provide an `onChange` handler that is called whenever the `<select>` is updated |

## Blocks

- default block: Pass in `<option>`/`SelectItemGroup` elements

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLSelectElement`.
Imports 
import TimePickerSelect from 'carbon-components-ember/components/time-picker/time-picker-select';

    @onChange={{@onChange}}
  >

Toggletip

components-toggletip · ./src/components/toggletip.stories.gts
A `Toggletip` is used to provide extra information about an element on the page. It renders a button that, when clicked, shows a popover with additional content. Unlike a `Tooltip`, its content can contain interactive elements like links and buttons, since it stays open until the user dismisses it (by clicking the button again, clicking outside, or pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd>). `Toggletip` yields a `Button` and `Content` component that coordinate the open/closed state and accessibility attributes between them. `ToggletipLabel` and `ToggletipActions` are standalone helpers for the label next to it and the actions row inside the content.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `ToggletipAlignment` |  | Specify how the toggletip should align with its trigger button. |
| `@defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the toggletip should be open by default. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `Button`: component
    - `Content`: component

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLSpanElement`.

Toolbar

ai-chat-toolbar · ./src/components/ai-chat/toolbar.stories.gts
`Toolbar` renders a horizontal action bar: a navigation area, a title, and a row of icon-button actions. Setting `@overflow` collapses actions that don't fit the available width into an overflow menu; actions marked `fixed` never overflow. The `navigation`, `title`, `fixedActions` and `decorator` named blocks mirror upstream's slots of the same names.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@actions` | `ToolbarAction[]` |  |  |
| `@overflow` | `boolean` |  | Enables responsive overflow: actions that don't fit the available width collapse into an overflow menu. When `false` (the default), all actions render inline in their given order, with no measurement and no overflow menu. |
| `@titleText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@nameText` | `string` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:navigation>`: The toolbar's leading navigation area.
- `<:title>`: Overrides the default title (built from `@titleText`/`@nameText`).
- `<:fixedActions>`: Actions that always stay visible, rendered after the overflow menu.
- `<:decorator>`: Upstream's own JSDoc calls this slot `toolbar-ai-label`, but its actual template renders `<slot name="decorator">` - this port matches the real behavior, not the stale doc comment.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import Toolbar from 'carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/toolbar';
Default story ok 
<Toolbar
  @actions={{actions}}
  @overflow={{true}}
  @titleText={{@titleText}}
  @nameText={{@nameText}}
  style={{style}}
>
  <:navigation>
    {{#if (eq args.navigation "home")}}
      <Tooltip @label="Home" @align="bottom-start">
        <Button
          @ghost={{true}}
          @iconOnly={{true}}
          @size="md"
          @onClick={{navClick}}
        >
          <Home @size={{16}} @svgClass="cds-aichat-story-icon" />
        </Button>
      </Tooltip>
    {{else if (eq args.navigation "back")}}
      <Tooltip @label="Back" @align="bottom-start">
        <Button
          @ghost={{true}}
          @iconOnly={{true}}
          @size="md"
          @onClick={{navClick}}
        >
          <ArrowLeft @size={{16}} @svgClass="cds-aichat-story-icon" />
        </Button>
      </Tooltip>
    {{else if (eq args.navigation "custom 1")}}
      <OverflowMenu @tooltip="Menu" @direction="bottom">
        <OverflowMenuItem @itemText="Stop app" />
        <OverflowMenuItem @itemText="Restart app" />
        <OverflowMenuItem @itemText="Rename app" />
        <OverflowMenuItem
          @itemText="Clone and move app"
          @disabled={{true}}
        />
        <OverflowMenuItem @itemText="Edit routes and access" />
        <OverflowMenuItem
          @itemText="Delete app"
          @hasDivider={{true}}
          @isDelete={{true}}
        />
      </OverflowMenu>
    {{else if (eq args.navigation "custom 2")}}
      <Button @size="md" @onClick={{navClick}}>test</Button>
    {{/if}}
  </:navigation>
  <:title>
    {{#if (eq args.titleSlot "default")}}
      <div style="white-space: nowrap;">
        Title
        <span class="cds--type-heading-compact-01">text</span>
      </div>
    {{else if (eq args.titleSlot "with truncation")}}
      <div>
        <span
          style="display: -webkit-box; overflow: hidden; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 1; line-height: normal; word-break: break-all;"
        >
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet
          <span class="cds--type-heading-compact-01">consectetur</span>
        </span>
      </div>
    {{/if}}
  </:title>
  <:fixedActions>
    {{#if (eq args.fixedActions "custom 1")}}
      <Button @size="md" @onClick={{fixedClick}}>test</Button>
    {{/if}}
  </:fixedActions>
</Toolbar>

Tooltip

components-tooltip · ./src/components/tooltip.stories.gts
Tooltips display additional information upon hover or focus. The information should be contextual, useful, and nonessential. A tooltip is attached to the element yielded in its default block and shows after a short delay on hover, or immediately on keyboard focus. Pressing `Escape` dismisses it. Use `@label` when the tooltip names the trigger (exposed as `aria-labelledby`), or `@description` when it adds extra information (exposed as `aria-describedby`). For rich content, use the `:content` block instead. Placement is controlled with `@align`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-left" \| "top-start" \| "top-right" \| "top-end" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-end" \| "left-bottom" \| "left-end" \| "left-top" \| "left-start" \| "right-bottom" \| "right-end" \| "right-top" \| "right-start"` |  | Where the tooltip is placed relative to the trigger |
| `@label` | `string` |  | Label text identifying the trigger. It names the trigger element through `aria-labelledby` (use it for icon-only triggers). |
| `@description` | `string` |  | Description text for the trigger, linked through `aria-describedby` |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Will auto-align the tooltip on open if it is not visible within the viewport (or `autoAlignBoundary`, if provided). |
| `@autoAlignBoundary` | `HTMLElement` |  | Specify a bounding element to be used for autoAlign calculations. The viewport is used by default. |
| `@closeOnActivation` | `boolean` |  | Close the tooltip when the trigger is activated (click, Enter, Space) |
| `@defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Render the tooltip open on initial render |
| `@dropShadow` | `boolean` |  | Render a drop shadow on the tooltip |
| `@enterDelayMs` | `number` |  | Delay in ms before the tooltip shows on hover |
| `@highContrast` | `boolean` |  | Render with the high contrast theme |
| `@leaveDelayMs` | `number` |  | Delay in ms before the tooltip hides after the pointer leaves |

## Blocks

- default block: The trigger element the tooltip is attached to
- `<:content>`: Custom tooltip content, used instead of

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLSpanElement`.

import Tooltip from 'carbon-components-ember/components/tooltip';

TreeView

components-treeview · ./src/components/tree-view.stories.gts
TreeView is used to render a hierarchical list of nested items that can be expanded or collapsed. `TreeView` and each node yield a bound `TreeNode` component that can be nested arbitrarily deep to build out the tree; select or activate a node by clicking on it. By default only a single node can be selected at a time. `@multiselect` allows selecting additional nodes by clicking while holding <kbd>Cmd</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>. `@onSelect` is called with the array of selected node ids and the node that triggered the change, and `@onActivate` with the id of the node that received keyboard/click focus. A disabled node can't be selected or focused (it is removed from the tab order) but still renders, dimmed; on a parent node its toggle caret stays usable so its descendants remain reachable.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@multiselect` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@selected` | `string[]` |  |  |
| `@active` | `string` |  |  |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "xs"` |  |  |
| `@onSelect` | `(selected: string[], node: TreeNode) => void` |  |  |
| `@onActivate` | `(active: string) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `TreeNode` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLUListElement`.

UIShell

components-ui-shell-header · ./src/components/ui-shell/header.stories.gts
The UI Shell is the structural framework of an application that houses navigational elements and page content, so users can move through an application consistently and predictably. Its `shell` block yields a `Header` (top bar with the product name, navigation, and global actions), a `Nav` (top-level navigation links and `HeaderMenu`s), a `Sidenav` (left-hand navigation panel), a `Switcher` and a `HeaderContainer`; the `content` block is the page content. The `Header` yields a `GlobalAction` into its `headerGlobal` block (icon buttons for search, notifications, the app switcher, ...) and a `HeaderPanel` into its `headerPanel` block. The `Sidenav` block yields `Menu`, `Divider`, `SideNavHeader`, `SideNavDetails`, `SideNavIcon` and `HeaderSideNavItems`, and its `footer` block a `Footer` toggle; wire the toggle to the same `@open`/`@onToggle` state as the `Header`'s menu button (or use `HeaderContainer`, which manages it).
API description 
## Blocks

- `<:shell>`
  - yields a hash:
    - `Header`: component
    - `Sidenav`: component
    - `Nav`: component
    - `Switcher`: component
    - `HeaderContainer`: component
- `<:content>`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports

UnorderedList

components-unorderedlist · ./src/components/unordered-list.stories.gts
Unordered lists are groupings of related content that have no priority. Each item is a `ListItem`: a single `<li>` with the styles it needs to work as a child of `OrderedList` or `UnorderedList`. It has no arguments of its own; any attributes passed to it (`id`, `class`, ...) are applied to the underlying `<li>`. A `ListItem` can contain a nested list (with `@nested={{true}}`) to build multi-level lists.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@nested` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@isExpressive` | `boolean` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `ListItem` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLUListElement`.
Imports 
import UnorderedList from 'carbon-components-ember/components/unordered-list';

VideoPlayer

ai-chat-video-player · ./src/components/ai-chat/video-player.stories.gts
`VideoPlayer` plays video for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat). It supports native `<video>` files (mp4, webm, HLS, DASH, ...) plus YouTube, Vimeo, and Kaltura URLs, auto-detected from `@source`. A source it doesn't recognize surfaces `@errorMessage` through the error state and `@onError` rather than failing silently.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@source` (required) | `string` |  | Video source URL (required). |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Video player'`. |
| `@playing` | `boolean` |  | Whether the video should be playing. Only reacted to on later change - the initial value is applied via provider autoplay. |
| `@aspectRatioPercentage` | `number` |  | Aspect ratio as a padding-top percentage. Defaults to `56.25` (16:9). |
| `@subtitleTracks` | `SubtitleTrack[]` |  | WebVTT caption/subtitle tracks - only honored by the native `<video>` provider, ignored by embed providers (matches upstream). |
| `@errorMessage` | `string` |  | Generic error message shown/reported regardless of the actual failure. Defaults to `'Failed to load video'`. |
| `@loadingStatusMessage` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Video player loading'`. |
| `@readyStatusMessage` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Video player ready'`. |
| `@loadingLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Loading'`. |
| `@readyLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Ready'`. |
| `@errorLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Error'`. |
| `@onReady` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onPlay` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onPause` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `@onError` | `(detail: { message: string; }) => void` |  |  |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import VideoPlayer from 'carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/video-player';
Default story ok 
{{#if args.useCard}}
  <AiChatCard @isFlush={{true}}>
    <:media>
      <VideoPlayer
        @source={{@source}}
        @playing={{false}}
        @aspectRatioPercentage={{56.25}}
        @ariaLabel="Video player"
        @subtitleTracks={{@subtitleTracks}}
        @errorMessage={{@errorMessage}}
        @onReady={{@onReady}}
        @onPlay={{@onPlay}}
        @onPause={{@onPause}}
        @onError={{@onError}}
      />

    <:body>

WorkspaceShell

ai-chat-workspace-shell · ./src/components/ai-chat/workspace-shell.stories.gts
Info
No description found. Write a jsdoc comment such as /** Component description */.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@autoCollapsibleHeader` | `boolean` |  | Enables automatic header collapsible behavior: the header yielded to the `header` block becomes collapsible whenever the body would otherwise have less room than the header itself takes up. |

## Blocks

- `<:toolbar>`
- `<:notification>`
- `<:header>`: Yields a `WorkspaceShellHeader` pre-bound with `@collapsible` driven by `@autoCollapsibleHeader` - use this instead of importing `WorkspaceShellHeader` directly to get the automatic behavior (same `WithBoundArgs` pattern `Layer` uses for its own ambient context).
  - yields `WorkspaceShellHeader` (component)
- `<:body>`
- `<:footer>`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import WorkspaceShell from 'carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/workspace-shell';
Default story ok 
<div style="display: flex; block-size: 40rem;">
  <WorkspaceShell
    @autoCollapsibleHeader={{false}}
    style="flex: 1;"
  >
    <:toolbar>
      <Toolbar
        @titleText="Title"
        @overflow={{true}}
        @actions={{toolbarActions}}
      />
    </:toolbar>
    <:notification>
      <Notification
        @display="inline"
        @kind="warning"
        @title="Title"
        @text="Message"
      />
    </:notification>
    <:header as |Header|>
      <Header
        @titleText="Title"
        @subTitleText="Sub title"
      >
        <:headerDescription>
          <div>
            Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed
            do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.
            Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco.
          </div>
          {{#if (eq args.headerDescription "withTags")}}
            <div style="display: flex; gap: 4px;">
              <Tag @size="sm" @type="gray">Tag</Tag>
              <Tag @size="sm" @type="gray">Tag</Tag>
              <Tag @size="sm" @type="gray">Tag</Tag>
              <Tag @size="sm" @type="gray">Tag</Tag>
              <Tag @size="sm" @type="gray">Tag</Tag>
            </div>
          {{/if}}
        </:headerDescription>
        <:headerAction>
          {{#if args.showHeaderAction}}
            <Button @type={{undefined}} @tertiary={{true}}>
              Edit Plan
              <Edit @size="16" @svgClass="cds--btn__icon" />
            </Button>
          {{/if}}
        </:headerAction>
      </Header>
    </:header>
    <:body>
      <WorkspaceShellBody>
        {{#if (eq args.bodyContent "long")}}
          <div>
            <p>
              Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
              Curabitur et velit sed erat faucibus blandit non nec felis.
              Nulla facilisi. Pellentesque nec finibus lectus. Vestibulum
              vitae sem eget lacus aliquam congue vitae ut elit.
            </p>
            <br />
            <AiChatCodeSnippet
              @code={{MULTILINE_CODE}}
              @language="typescript"
              @highlight={{true}}
            />
            <br />
            <p>
              Fusce egestas sapien id sem luctus, nec hendrerit velit
              elementum. In in justo a nunc accumsan vestibulum. Quisque
              ut interdum est. Proin id felis ac justo blandit dictum.
              Suspendisse in tellus a risus fermentum volutpat vel quis
              leo. Curabitur varius, libero at pulvinar suscipit, urna
              nisi volutpat felis, sed maximus diam eros non metus.
            </p>
          </div>
        {{else}}
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do
          eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut
          enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco.
        {{/if}}
      </WorkspaceShellBody>
    </:body>
    <:footer>
      {{#if footerActions}}
        <WorkspaceShellFooter
          @actions={{footerActions}}
          @onClick={{@onFooterAction}}
        />
      {{/if}}
    </:footer>
  </WorkspaceShell>
</div>

WorkspaceShellHeader

ai-chat-workspace-shell-header · ./src/components/ai-chat/workspace-shell-header.stories.gts
Info
No description found. Write a jsdoc comment such as /** Component description */.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@titleText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@subTitleText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@collapsible` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, the header renders as a `<details>`/`<summary>` that starts collapsed and can be toggled open. When `false` (the default), the header always renders fully expanded. |
| `@onToggle` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new open state whenever a collapsible header is toggled. |

## Blocks

- `<:headerDescription>`: Extra description content, rendered after `@subTitleText`.
- `<:headerAction>`: Action content (e.g. buttons), rendered outside the collapsible area.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement | HTMLDetailsElement`.

# Carbon Components Ember

An Ember implementation of IBM's [Carbon Design System](https://carbondesignsystem.com),
kept in parity with [`@carbon/react`](https://react.carbondesignsystem.com).

## Installation

```sh
pnpm add carbon-components-ember @carbon/styles
pnpm add -D sass
```

### Compatibility

- **Ember:** tested against `ember-source` 7 (the current release), and in CI
  against the beta and alpha channels too.
- **Apps:** it's a v2 addon. Embroider/Vite apps work as-is; classic ember-cli
  apps need `ember-auto-import` 2. Apps compile its stylesheets, so they need
  `sass`.

Load Carbon's styles and the addon's own stylesheet once, in your app's
entry point:

```ts
import "@carbon/styles/css/styles.css";
import "carbon-components-ember/styles.scss";
```

Some components render elsewhere in the page, so add their two targets to
your application template:

```gts
<template>
  {{outlet}}

  {{! Dropdown, Select and OverflowMenu menus }}
  <div id="ember-basic-dropdown-wormhole"></div>
  {{! The confirmation dialog of a @danger Button or Icon }}
  <div id="carbon-components-dialog-id"></div>
</template>
```

## Usage

Import components straight into your `.gts` templates:

```gts
import { Button } from "carbon-components-ember/components";

<template>
  <Button @type="primary">Save</Button>
</template>
```

Services are namespaced under `carbon.`:

```ts
import { service } from "@ember/service";

class MyComponent {
  @service("carbon.notifications") notifications;
}
```

Every component page in the sidebar is generated from the component's own
Glint signature: the args table, blocks and element come straight from the
source, and each story doubles as a browser test. Stories follow Carbon
React's: the same pages, names and variants, and each story file lists any
React story it can't match yet.

## Use with AI agents

The package ships an [agent skill](https://agentskills.io) for coding agents:
how to use the components, how Carbon's React-based docs and designs carry
over to Ember, and these docs for the version your app has installed. With pnpm 12.11 or later, approve
it once with `pnpm approve carbon-components-ember`. The
[README](https://github.com/IBM/carbon-components-ember#use-with-ai-agents)
covers the requirements, and the steps for TanStack Intent, npm and Yarn.

[`carbon-components-ember-mcp`](https://github.com/IBM/carbon-components-ember/tree/main/carbon-components-ember-mcp#readme)
serves the same docs over MCP, and gives agents the skill's instructions when
they connect. Add it from your app's directory, for example in Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add carbon-components-ember -- npx -y carbon-components-ember-mcp
```
